title: Director, Silicon Logical Design
descriptionHtml:
About Graphcore 

At Graphcore, we’re building the future of AI compute.

We’re a team of semiconductor, software and AI experts, with deep experience in creating the complete AI compute stack - from silicon and software to infrastructure at datacenter scale.

As part of the SoftBank Group, backed by significant long-term investment, we are delivering key technology into the fast-growing SoftBank AI ecosystem.

To meet the vast and exciting AI opportunity, Graphcore is expanding its teams around the world.

We are bringing together the brightest minds to solve the toughest problems, in a place where everyone has the opportunity to make an impact on the company, our products and the future of artificial intelligence.

Job Summary 

We are seeking a Director of Silicon Logical Design to lead and scale our Logical Design group within the Silicon department. This role is accountable for the overall strategy, technical direction, execution quality and team development for Graphcores microarchitecture and RTL design efforts. 

The Director will be responsible for ensuring that our logical design methodologies, architectures and RTL implementations meet world class standards for performance, power, area, and schedule. This leader will partner closely with Architecture, Physical Design, Verification, DFT and Program Management teams to ensure successful, predictable silicon delivery aligned with Graphcores long term product roadmap. 

The Team 

The Logical Design team deliver the micro-architecture and RTL that realise our advanced chip architectures. As Director, you will guide this multi site team, strengthen cross functional collaboration, and drive the evolution of our design flows and capabilities. 

Responsibilities and Duties 

Leadership & Strategy 

  • Define and execute the strategic roadmap for Logical Design, ensuring alignment with Graphcores silicon and product strategy. 
  • Lead, grow and mentor a high performing RTL/micro architecture design organisation. 
  • Establish and implement best in class design methodologies, documentation standards and quality metrics. 
  • Drive continuous improvement across team structure, workflows, tooling, and design processes. 

Technical Ownership 

  • Provide technical oversight of micro architecture specification and RTL development across all major blocks and subsystems. 
  • Guide architectural feasibility studies, contribute to architectural trade offs and micro architecture definition. 
  • Oversee the integration of third party IP, complex application specific blocks, and high performance custom designs. 
  • Ensure robust design sign off through high quality linting, synthesis, CDC/RDC, timing closure and coverage metrics. 

Cross-Functional Collaboration 

  • Partner closely with Physical Design, Verification, DFT, Architecture and Program Management teams to ensure cohesive planning and execution. 
  • Foster strong communication across teams and global sites, ensuring alignment on priorities, risks and deliverables. 
  • Support silicon bring-up and debug efforts by providing expert guidance and deep understanding of RTL behaviour and architecture. 

Execution & Delivery 

  • Own delivery of high quality, on schedule RTL for multiple parallel silicon programs. 
  • Establish scalable project planning and tracking practices, including resource planning and risk mitigation. 
  • Champion design automation and infrastructure improvements to accelerate productivity and improve design quality. 

Essential Skills & Experience 

  • Degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or a related field; advanced degree preferred. 
  • Extensive experience in digital logical design, micro-architecture and RTL development for large scale, high performance silicon projects. 
  • Proven success leading and developing technical teams in a semiconductor environment. 
  • Deep expertise in SystemVerilog or VHDL and familiarity with modern digital design flows. 
  • Strong ability to diagnose and resolve complex design issues, including via scripting/programming (Python, Tcl, etc.). 
  • Demonstrated excellence in cross functional leadership and communication across global teams. 
  • Strong organisational skills with ability to manage multiple priorities and drive execution in fast-paced environments. 

Desirable Experience 

  • Processor or accelerator micro architecture. 
  • High-speed serial interfaces and complex, high bandwidth IP blocks. 
  • Arithmetic pipeline design and floating point datapaths. 
  • Advanced synthesis, timing analysis, power analysis, and logical equivalence checking. 
  • Design-for-test methodologies. 
  • Power integrity and silicon device level understanding. 
  • Experience with silicon bring-up and post-silicon validation. 
  • Program planning and multi-project execution leadership.

title: Division Operations Senior Associate, Undersea Dominance
department: Maritime & Maneuver Dominance : Undersea Dominance - Engineering & Operations
descriptionHtml:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

Maritime Division Operations Senior Associate

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Maritime Division, one of Anduril's fastest growing divisions, has assembled a diverse team of experts in software, robotics, artificial intelligence, sensor fusion, and data analysis to create software and hardware solutions that radically evolve the capabilities of our customers. We are fielding the next generation of autonomous systems to tackle the extremely challenging industry demands of maritime operations. Anduril has brought to market a unique, ultra-long-range, full-ocean-depth underwater vessel platform and a completely refreshed maritime vehicle and flexible manufacturing architecture that scales from "small" to "extra-large" vehicle sizes. Today, Anduril is executing on billion-dollar contracts while simultaneously performing Robot-as-a-Service (RaaS) AUV operations.

We are seeking to sustain our early successes with deep investment in an expanded product portfolio. These products, including Dive-XL, Dive-LD, Copperhead, Seabed Sentry, and other unannounced systems, will deliver a coherent system-of-systems, enabling the end-to-end conduct of a variety of autonomous missions in the maritime domain. If you are passionate about solving problems that have real impact and working on systems that directly contribute to achieving national strategic priorities for Australia and its allies, we want you to join Anduril's Maritime Division and help us build the future of defence capability.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Division Operations Senior Associate to join our rapidly growing Maritime Division Operations team in Sydney, Australia. In this role, you will be responsible for supporting our internal business lines as well as the entire division. The Maritime Division Operations team is a small but mighty team of talented business generalists who enable the division to scale through hyper-growth while breaking as few things as possible.

We're looking for someone to help us build out the business infrastructure required to grow this into Anduril's largest division over the next few years. Our goal is to fundamentally reshape the way future peer to peer conflicts are fought by developing next generation undersea and surface capabilities, such as our XL-AUV, Copperhead, and Seabed Sentry platforms.

This is an operator role, not an advisory one. You won't be writing recommendations for someone else to execute. You'll own the outcome. You'll work closely with division leadership in Sydney and partner across time zones with teams in the U.S., so you'll need to be comfortable operating with a high degree of autonomy.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Lead various strategic initiatives and special projects, as directed by Directors and the Chief of Staff, to establish scalable operations across the portfolio, ranging from strategic and international finance, production and supply chain, facilities and real estate, security, etc
  • Act as the connective tissue between efforts related to the design, development, and implementation of new processes, strategy, and execution plans
  • Build the models, trackers, and dashboards the division runs on (headcount, financial, facilities, and production) and keep them alive, not just stand them up
  • Coordinate and prepare for executive leadership meetings, including setting agendas, tracking action items, and ensuring follow-through
  • Support internal team operations like new employee onboarding, all hands, internal business reviews, and other division-wide events so that we rapidly ramp new employees and maintain a culture of "doing things differently"
  • Support our corporate planning cycle by helping to build out and monitor performance against goals, financial plans, and headcount plans so we can hit our aggressive growth targets
  • Establish the operating model and battle rhythm for a rapidly growing team with an emphasis on cross-division coordination and repeatable execution patterns

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • You have 3+ years of experience in consulting, operations, finance, or general business analysis in a commercial, government, or defence industry environment
  • You can clearly articulate why defence, and why Anduril. You have a genuine conviction in the mission, not just interest in the technology
  • You have personally built something operational (a process, tool, or system) that other people used day-to-day. Not advised on it. Built it.
  • You love solving complex, ambiguous, cross-functional problems in a people-centric way, and can point to a time you drove alignment across teams with competing priorities without direct authority
  • You're a clear, structured communicator, in writing and in the room, with senior leaders and engineers alike
  • You manage stakeholders at every level, from engineers and technicians on the floor to program managers, functional leads, Directors, and executives, plus partner teams in the U.S. You build trust, tailor your message to the audience, manage up, push back when needed, and keep people aligned when you aren't in the room
  • You're highly competent with AI tools (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot) and use them every day to analyse data, draft, research, and build. You know their limits, check the output, and can show us real examples where AI made your work faster or better
  • You're both high ownership and low ego, approaching everything with strong outcome orientation and high humility
  • You get energy from being a thought partner for others and it excites you to spend time translating operational problems into data problems, and to then going and executing on them
  • Strong hands-on Excel skills (modelling, data manipulation, pivot tables). Be ready to show us what you've built
  • You're discerning and an incredibly fast learner. When something doesn't check every box, you figure it out
  • You're tactical and don't only sit at a 30,000 foot level
  • Must be an Australian citizen and able to obtain and maintain an Australian Government security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree or higher in business, engineering, law, or a related field
  • Background in a high-growth tech company, or in corporate finance, accounting, or strategy
  • Exposure to supply chain, production, or workforce planning problems
  • Experience with data and analytics tooling including Excel and beyond (e.g. SQL, Tableau, Power BI, Palantir Foundry)
  • Hands-on experience building AI-enabled tools or automations (e.g. custom GPTs or Claude projects, agents, scripts, Power Automate, or LLM APIs) and an understanding of how to use them safely in a security-conscious environment

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: 

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

  • No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

  • Please always verify communications:
    • Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an ----- address.
    • Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to

    • Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is ----- before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

    • What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to 

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/. 

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

title: Ehrenamt · remote · 4–6 Std./Woche: Projektleiter / Projektmanager (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Du hast Freude daran, Ideen in konkrete Projekte zu verwandeln, Menschen zusammenzubringen und Vorhaben von der Planung bis zur Umsetzung zu begleiten? Vielleicht bringst du bereits Erfahrung im Projektmanagement, in der Organisationsentwicklung oder in der Zusammenarbeit mit unterschiedlichen Teams mit.

Bei uns übernimmst du Verantwortung für spannende Projekte mit gesellschaftlicher Wirkung. Eines davon ist DEHIB Masterminds, unser Qualifizierungs- und Leadership-Programm, das ehrenamtliches Engagement mit fachlicher Weiterbildung, Persönlichkeitsentwicklung und praktischer Führungserfahrung verbindet.

Du musst nicht jede Projektmanagementmethode beherrschen. Viel wichtiger sind uns Eigeninitiative, Organisationstalent und die Fähigkeit, Menschen für gemeinsame Ziele zu begeistern

Gleich vorweg: Das ist ein Ehrenamt

Die Aufgabe ist unbezahlt und begründet kein Arbeitsverhältnis. Wir suchen Menschen, die ihre Fähigkeiten, Erfahrungen und Ideen einbringen möchten, weil sie gesellschaftlich etwas bewegen und gleichzeitig selbst Verantwortung übernehmen wollen.

Wer wir sind

Der Deutsche Hilfsbund e.V. (DEHIB) bündelt Hilfsorganisationen und bringt sie mit Menschen aus Wirtschaft, Politik und Wissenschaft zusammen, damit soziales Engagement mehr bewirkt.

Wir verbinden Verbände, schaffen professionelle Strukturen und bauen bundesweit eine Plattform für gesellschaftliche Wirkung auf.

Mit Projekten wie DEHIB Masterminds entwickeln wir innovative Ansätze, um ehrenamtliches Engagement zu professionalisieren, Kompetenzen sichtbar zu machen und Menschen neue Entwicklungsperspektiven zu eröffnen.

Damit aus diesen Ideen erfolgreiche Projekte werden, brauchen wir Menschen, die Verantwortung übernehmen und dich.

Deine Aufgaben

· Projekte eigenständig steuern: Projekte von der ersten Planung über die operative Umsetzung bis zum erfolgreichen Abschluss begleiten

· DEHIB Masterminds mitgestalten: Beim Aufbau und der Weiterentwicklung unseres Qualifizierungs- und Leadership-Programms mitwirken

· Projektplanung und Organisation: Ziele, Arbeitspakete, Meilensteine, Zuständigkeiten und Zeitpläne definieren und koordinieren

title: Embedded Banking Financial Crime Oversight Lead
descriptionHtml:
Trust unlocks our greatest potential.

For decades, the clearing of payments remained unchanged and unchallenged. We asked, what if there was a better way? What if we could make banking infrastructure faster, safer, more reliable, and easier to access for all? Here is where you can think radically and responsibly to find the best solution.

What happens when you know you’re inherently trusted? Trust creates safety. Safety encourages you to be brave, to challenge, to fail, to try new things and to execute. At ClearBank everything revolves around trust. We’re not expected to earn it, but we are expected not to break it. We’re trusted to own it. To solve issues in the moment. To know a good risk when we see one, and the judgement to know that ‘can’ doesn’t always mean you ‘should’.

What you can expect:

ClearBank is a place where you can do things differently and challenge the status quo. We will give you a high level of autonomy and transparency, and we trust you to make the right decisions for the bank.

If that excites you, how about joining our Embedded Banking Financial Crime Oversight team as an Embedded Banking Financial Crime Oversight Lead? Reporting to the Head of Embedded Banking Financial Crime Oversight, you will coordinate thorough assessments of new Embedded Banking Partners to evaluate their financial crime controls, with emphasis on outsourced processes. You must understand their Operating Model, including systems, processes, and sub-contractors. After onboarding, you will monitor these partners' financial crime controls, assess risks using ClearBank’s taxonomy and relevant data, and ensure compliance with the Oversight model, including leading governance sessions.

Your role includes:

  • Ensuring and overseeing compliance with all internal policies, standards, industry guidance and regulation

  • Leading the completion of the Financial Crime Systems and Controls Assessments for all new Embedded Banking relationships in accordance with policies, standards, and procedures

  • Responsible for the monitoring and oversight of existing Embedded Banking Partners in accordance with standards and procedures from a financial crime perspective.

  • Ensuring all oversight activities are completed in accordance with the Oversight Model

  • Continuously assessing and updating financial crime aspects of Embedded Banking Partners Risk and Control registries

  • Defining and reporting internal and external Key Risk Indicators enabling data driven performance monitoring

  • Chairing all Embedded Banking Partner financial crime governance sessions where required

  • Responsible for maintenance of Embedded Banking Partner Management Procedures covering Onboarding & Oversight from a financial crime perspective

  • Supporting the delivery of relevant aspects of the Embedded Banking change programme

  • Supporting the development and implementation of new financial crime systems and controls

  • Building and maintaining knowledge of all relevant legislation, regulatory changes, and industry best practice

What you’ll bring:

To excel in this role, you’ll also need:

  • Significant expertise in risk and control frameworks and compliance with regulatory standards specifically in relation to financial crime, especially in relation to outsourcing of those controls

  • Audit, assurance or consultancy background with significant experience in the oversight and review/assessment of the adequacy and effectiveness of financial crime control frameworks

  • Strong understanding of sectors such as money remittance, electronic money, APIs, Cryptocurrency firms, and merchant acquirers is a plus

  • Experience dealing with complex and varied business models

  • Self-starter, able to work independently when needed, and to prioritise tasks

  • Ability to communicate and negotiate with key stakeholders and customers

  • Strong attention to detail and good judgement

  • Work to tight deadlines, whilst maintaining high level of quality and competency

  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities

Regretfully we are not able to sponsor applicants for immigration purposes at the current time.

What makes a great ClearBank team member? Does this sound like you?

  • You focus on solutions and positive outcomes, thinking radically and responsibly to find the best result for our customers, your colleagues and the bank;

  • You actively seek feedback from others to drive your growth and development, always assuming positive intent from others and develop strong, trusting relationships you’re your colleagues and customers: you really, genuinely care;

  • You always strive for the highest quality, but you know that done is better than perfect; you welcome a challenge knowing that they learn as you go and iterate;

  • ‘I’ before ’we’, isn’t in your vocabulary

If this sounds like you then we encourage you to dust off that CV and apply!

What we offer in return:

  • We're flexible – We support a culture of flexibility which allows our employees to achieve a strong work-life balance.

  • Offices – Work in a way that works for you – whether that’s in the London office, at home, or hybrid.

  • Holiday – 27 days of annual leave per year, plus bank holidays.

  • Holiday buy/sell - Buy or sell up to five days of annual leave each year and shape your year around what matters most.

  • Work abroad – You have the flexibility to work outside of the UK for up to 30 days in a rolling 12-month period.

  • Socials – Regular social events open to all.

  • Holiday swap – Option to swap your bank holidays to any other day of your choice.

  • Wellbeing – 24/7 employee assistance programme including mental health support, life assurance and income protection.

  • Bigger than ClearBank – Take a couple of days per year to do something that matters to you.

  • Healthy living – Private healthcare and discounted dental cover, with employee perks and discounts.

  • Family – Enhanced family-friendly leave.

  • Personal development – We offer personal development budgets, opportunities to take part in role-related training and unlimited LinkedIn Learning.

And not forgetting the biggest benefit of all. The opportunity to be part of an incredible team that’s building a tech-bank fit for the future.

A little bit more about us! 

ClearBank is Where You Can belong: 

At ClearBank we think about Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DE&I) a lot. Not because we think we should. But because we know we should – how else can we build a happy workforce and be successful as a business. We’re committed to making sure our teams reflect society. And we put energy and effort into making this a place where everyone feels at home, where they’re given the trust and encouragement to do their very best work. Here are some of the things we’re most proud of: 

  • 42% of our senior management roles are held by women 

  • Our enhanced family leave policies

  • Launching our partnership with Code First Girls 

  • Increasing awareness of neurodiversity in the workplace through our partnership with the Inclusive Group 

Our hiring process and what you can expect:

Application: a member of our talent acquisition team will review your application against the key requirements for the role and let you know within two weeks whether you’re moving forward to the next stage; 

Screening: You’ll spend 30-45 minutes speaking to one of our recruiters learning more about the role and ClearBank, and we’ll get it know more about you, your experience and how your skills align with the role (this will be via phone or Teams video call). You can expect to hear back from us within seven days following this meeting (if things are taking longer than expected, we’ll let you know that too); 

First Interview: You’ll spend one hour with a member of our hiring team focusing on your skills, competencies and your ways of working at the same time we’ll give you time to ask more questions about the role, the team and learn more about the ClearBank culture. This will be via Teams.  

Second Interview: This will be a competency-based interview with one or more members of our team.

Final Stage: You will have a final meeting with the Head of Department. This will be around 45-60 minutes.  

Offer: Congratulations! Get ready to transform banking forever! 

Our commitment to you as a candidate: 

We will always try our best to get back to you within seven days of your interview whether you’ve been successful or not and provide you with feedback. Sometimes things take a little longer, so we may not have a decision to share but we will get it touch to let you know we need a little more time.  

We’re unable to provide specific individual feedback at the application or screening stage but know that your application was reviewed and considered carefully.  

We wish you the best of luck with your application and maybe we’ll be celebrating your new role at ClearBank soon!  

Equal Opportunities

ClearBank is committed to ensuring equal opportunities throughout every stage of the recruitment process. ClearBank recognises that diversity is vital to the long-term success of the business in the communities and markets in which it operates. ClearBank is also a firm believer that an inclusive culture fosters greater employee engagement and collaboration. 

ClearBank strives for diversity and inclusion of all forms, including (but not limited to): gender, age, educational and professional background, disability, gender reassignment, marital or civil partner status, pregnancy or maternity, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief and sexual orientation. 

As part of the Company’s commitment to equal employment opportunity, we provide reasonable adjustments, to candidates during the recruitment process, including to individuals with disabilities. We want to create a safe space that welcomes everyone so please let us know how we can accommodate you. In case you have any accessibility requirements you can share that with our Talent Acquisition team prior to your interview stage, if applicable. 

The legal bit

By submitting your CV to ClearBank Limited you are providing your consent for us to use the information you provide for recruitment purposes. For more information on how we manage your data go and check out our Candidate Privacy Notice on the ClearBank website to see how we process, manage and look after your data. You are also allowing us to communicate with you by email and telephone for recruitment purposes.

title: Embedded Software Engineer (LDN)
descriptionHtml:
For over four decades, Cirrus Logic has been propelled by the top engineers in mixed-signal processing. Our rockstar team thrives on solving complex challenges with innovative end-user solutions for the world's top consumer brands. Cirrus Logic is also known for its award-winning culture, built on a foundation of inclusion and fairness, meaningful community engagement, and delivering enjoyable employee experiences at every turn. But we couldn’t do it without our extraordinary workforce – and that’s where you come in. Join our team and help us continue to make Cirrus Logic an exceptional place to grow your career!
We’re looking for an Embedded Software Engineer who thrives close to the hardware and enjoys building high-performance, reliable firmware for DSP architecture and microcontrollers (e.g., RISC V and Arm Cortex M/A). You’ll design and implement real-time embedded software, optimize compute-heavy pipelines, and collaborate with hardware and systems teams to bring products from concept to production. This role suits someone who can move comfortably between architecture/design, low-level firmware, and performance tuning—especially where latency, throughput, power, and determinism matter.
Key Responsibilities:
  • Design, implement, and maintain embedded firmware for DSP cores and MCUs (RISC V and/or Arm).
  • Build and optimize real-time signal-processing pipelines (fixed-point and/or floating-point), potentially including FFTs, filters, modulation/demodulation, codecs, feature extraction, or control loops.
  • Develop firmware using a mix of C/C++ (and selective assembly where appropriate), with strong focus on performance, memory, and power optimization.
  • Work with SoC/board peripherals: DMA, timers, SPI, I²C, UART, I²S/TDM, PWM, GPIO, and relevant bus fabrics.
  • Bring up new hardware: boot flows, clocks, memory maps, interrupt vectors, peripheral init, and early validation.
  • Implement and debug drivers and RTOS components (e.g., Zephyr or equivalent), including task scheduling, synchronization primitives, and ISR design.
  • Develop test strategies: unit tests, hardware-in-the-loop tests, test automation, and manufacturing/production diagnostics.
  • Use debugging/profiling tools: JTAG/SWD, logic analyzers, oscilloscopes, trace (ETM/ITM), and cycle-accurate profiling when available.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with hardware, FPGA/ASIC, systems, and application teams to define requirements and interfaces.
  • Contribute documentation: architecture notes, interface specs, timing budgets, work packages, and bring-up guides.
  • Participate in code reviews and help establish best practices for embedded quality, safety, and maintainability.

    • Required Skills and Qualifications:
  • Strong professional experience developing embedded firmware in C/C++ for MCUs and/or DSPs.
  • Hands-on experience with RISC V and/or Arm architecture (Cortex M/A), including interrupts, memory, caches, and performance characteristics.
  • Solid understanding of embedded software fundamentals:
  • register-level programming, memory-mapped I/O
  • concurrency (ISRs, RTOS tasks), race conditions, timing determinism
  • fixed-point arithmetic, numerical precision, and overflow/underflow management
  • Proven ability to optimize firmware: cycle counting, memory layout, DMA usage, cache behavior, minimizing latency and jitter.
  • Comfortable with toolchains and build systems:
  • GCC/LLVM-based toolchains, cross-compilation
  • CMake/Make, Meson, linker scripts, map files
  • Strong debugging skills with hardware and firmware:
  • JTAG/SWD debugging
  • root-cause analysis of timing and performance issues
  • Source control expertise (Git) and disciplined engineering practices (code reviews, CI).

    • Preferred Skills and Qualifications:
  • Languages: C, C++, (optional) assembly, Python for test tooling/scripts
  • Architectures: RISC V, Arm Cortex M/A, DSP cores
  • RTOS/OS: Zephyr, embedded Linux (optional)
  • Tools: JTAG/SWD debuggers, GDB, OpenOCD/J-Link, logic analyzer, oscilloscope, trace tools
  • Practices: profiling, timing analysis, unit/integration testing, CI/CD for embedded
  • Experience with common DSP libraries/techniques (e.g., CMSIS-DSP, vendor DSP libs) and SIMD/vector optimization patterns.
  • Experience with Zephyr, or embedded Linux on Arm.
  • Familiarity with bootloaders, secure boot, OTA update mechanisms, and field diagnostics.
  • Understanding of digital communications, or audio, processing domains.
  • Exposure to safety/security standards (e.g., MISRA C/C++, IEC 61508, ISO 26262)
    • This Newbury or London based role is a hybrid remote position and will follow a 2 day in-office work schedule, with in-office days based on business needs and team preference. You must be based within commutable distance of the work location listed on the job posting, or willing to relocate prior to beginning employment with Cirrus Logic. #LI-PD1 #LI-Hybrid
    Export control restrictions based upon applicable laws and regulations would prohibit candidates who are nationals of certain embargoed countries from working in this position without Cirrus Logic first obtaining an export license. Candidates for this role must be able to access technical data without a requirement for an export license. We are unable to sponsor or obtain export licenses for this role.
    At Cirrus Logic, we believe that diversity drives innovation, and we are committed to encouraging an open and collaborative culture where different approaches, ideas, and points of view are respected and valued. We aim to promote a workplace where everyone can contribute irrespective of race, colour, national origin, religion or belief, gender or gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, pregnancy status, or disability.

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

We’reCheckout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.


We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.

The Role

We are looking for an experienced IT Engineer II to join Checkout’s IT Engineering team, supporting Workplace Technology. In this generalist role, you will work across the services and platforms managed by the team, helping colleagues get the technology they need while keeping those services secure, reliable, and easy to use.

You will contribute across areas such as identity and access, end-user devices, collaboration and productivity platforms, IT assets and licences, and office technology. You are not expected to be a subject matter expert in every product. Instead, you bring strong technical foundations, depth in one or more areas, and the curiosity to build working knowledge across the wider portfolio.

At this level, you can confidently resolve all but the most complex problems affecting the team. You will own operational outcomes, deliver small-to-medium projects independently, and work with colleagues and stakeholders to improve the services we provide across Checkout.

How You’ll Make an Impact

  • Cross-Portfolio Service Ownership: Administer and improve services across the Workplace Technology portfolio. This may include Okta, Google Workspace, Atlassian, macOS and Windows endpoint management through tools such as Jamf and Microsoft Intune, IT asset and licence processes, and office technology.

  • Identity and Access: Support secure identity lifecycle and access management, including joiner, mover, and leaver activities, single sign-on, group and role administration, and least-privilege access.

  • End-User Technology: Help manage and support company endpoints and workplace services. Apply approved configurations and security controls, troubleshoot issues, and contribute to a consistent employee experience across platforms.

  • Platform Administration: Configure and maintain team-managed applications and services. Learn unfamiliar platforms quickly, follow established governance, and identify when a change needs specialist or security review.

  • Operational Excellence: Provide dependable operational support, maintain clear documentation and runbooks, and help the team improve service quality, reliability, and supportability.

  • Incident and Change Management: Own incidents through the full lifecycle, from triage, prioritisation, and stakeholder communication through safe service restoration, root-cause analysis, and follow-up actions. Maintain accurate incident records, capture decisions and remediation, and document recurring issues and operational procedures in clear, current runbooks and knowledge articles. Plan and implement changes safely, with appropriate testing, approvals, and rollback plans.

  • Project Delivery: Plan and deliver small-to-medium technical projects, coordinating with stakeholders and other teams to manage dependencies, risks, and outcomes.

  • Automation and Improvement: Identify repeatable manual work and service friction. Propose or build appropriately controlled automation and simpler workflows to reduce toil and improve consistency.

  • Asset and Licence Management: Support accurate technology inventory, licence administration, and lifecycle processes, helping the team make effective and responsible use of its tools and equipment.

  • Knowledge Sharing: Share learning across the team, contribute to onboarding and operational guidance, and support colleagues as they develop their technical skills.

What We’re Looking For

  • Experience: Typically 2-3+ years in IT engineering, workplace technology, systems administration, or a similar technical role.

  • Technical Breadth: Practical experience supporting or administering a range of workplace technology services. You have a strong foundation in at least one relevant area and are motivated to build capability across others.

  • Relevant Platforms: Experience with some of the following is useful: identity and access management (for example, Okta and SSO); Google Workspace; Atlassian products; macOS or Windows endpoint management (for example, Jamf or Microsoft Intune); SaaS administration; IT asset or licence management; or office technology. You do not need experience with every product listed.

  • Security Mindset: Understand the importance of least privilege, secure configuration, data protection, auditability, and careful change management. You know when to escalate a risk or seek specialist guidance.

  • Problem Solving: Take a logical, evidence-led approach to troubleshooting. Explain technical options and trade-offs clearly, and distinguish between immediate mitigation and long-term resolution.

  • Ownership: Take responsibility for work from investigation through resolution and follow-up. Care about the long-term health of the services you support, not only closing individual requests.

  • Communication: Work effectively with colleagues, stakeholders, and technical teams. Translate technical detail into clear updates and provide helpful, user-focused support.

  • Adaptability: Comfortable working across a varied technology estate, learning new tools, and balancing planned delivery with operational priorities in a changing environment.

  • Teamwork: Share knowledge, ask for help when needed, and contribute positively to a team that works across multiple technical domains.

title: Engineering Leader
descriptionHtml:
About Kernel

Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?

Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.

Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.

Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent KERN ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Checkout already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them.

We have raised $20M from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing 5x YoY.

The Role

You'll be a player-coach engineering leader with a spike in technical strategy, you'll own engineering delivery for your team end-to-end - from developing exceptional engineers to solving some of our most difficult engineering problems & setting technical direction.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll spend roughly 20% of your time contributing code and 80% leading your team, with that ratio shifting as we scale.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build, hire, and develop a high-performing engineering team

  • Help set technical direction and architecture decisions

  • Work with the engineering to tackle some of our most difficult problems

  • Own engineering delivery with an emphasis on velocity

  • Collaborate closely with Product on roadmap and prioritisation

  • Write code when needed so you'll stay close to the product

The Opportunity

We are in the unique situation that our commercial traction is ahead of our product. You’ll play a leading role in moving towards automation in a way that enables us to rapidly scale with increased complexity and specific customer nuances.

About You

  • You have extensive experience in architecting enterprise-level systems, delivering on ambitious product visions, and building world class engineering teams.

  • You have worked at high-growth businesses, and might have previously started your own company.

  • You are highly analytical, and thinking proactively through the implications of your decisions, but also have high conviction and understand the importance of moving at pace and shipping often.

  • You have previously led engineering at a company from its earliest stages, and don’t shy away from the manager role - you know what great looks like, and want to help engineers grow.

Essential Experience

  • 8+ years software engineering experience

  • Track record of hiring and developing strong engineers

  • Strong production systems background - you've built and scaled things that matter, and you’ve done something hard and lived to tell the tale

  • Proven experience in distributed systems

  • Experience operating autonomously in small, high-velocity environments - ideally in a startup

  • Experience working in a data-focused company or closely alongside a data engineering/ML team - data is core to what we're building at Kernel, and you will play a key role in shaping how we grow that capability

Nice-to-Have:

  • Scaled an engineering team through a growth phase (5 → 20+ engineers), or from Series A to Series C

  • Technical depth across the stack: NodeJS, Postgres, TypeScript, Kubernetes AI-driven or data-heavy product experience

  • Understanding of LLMs (e.g., RAG, prompt engineering, evals)

  • CRM data models or workflow automation knowledge

  • Hands-on Data Engineering or ML Engineering experience - as data becomes an increasingly large part of what we do, this would be a great asset for us to have

⚠️ This role may not be for you if you:

  • Insist on shipping pixel-perfect code

  • Prefer managing from a distance without technical involvement

  • Need extensive process and structure before making decisions

❌ This role is definitely not for you:

  • If you over-rely on AI coding tools (Cursor, Claude Code) to the point where you don’t read or understand your own code

  • If you on the other hand don’t understand how these tools (Cursor, Claude Code, etc.) can be force multipliers for senior engineers if used correctly

  • If you prefer fully remote work

  • If you don’t like early-stage startup pace

  • If you’re seeking a purely ‘hands-off’ role

Tech Stack

  • Backend: AWS, NodeJS, TypeScript, Postgres, Clickhouse, Kubernetes

  • Frontend: NextJS, TypeScript, Tailwind

You don't need to know everything, but you should be comfortable diving into any part of the stack.

What We Offer

We will do our best to offer you a ride of a lifetime. It will not be easy, but it will be thrilling.

  • 💰 Salary: £130,000 – £170,000 + equity

  • 🗓️ 24 days holiday per year + bank holidays

  • 🥕 £450 Monthly Office Dinner Allowance

  • ✈️ 2 weeks work-from-anywhere

  • 🍼 Generous parental leave policy

  • 💼 Pension plan

  • 💻 Top-spec equipment and central London office

  • 🎉 Team events and dinners

  • 🚀 Work directly with the founders to scale the systems that power enterprise AI

  • 🏆 High-autonomy, high-trust environment with a small team shipping at pace

🎫 Visas & Relocation

We sponsor visas for exceptional candidates and provide relocation support for those moving to London.

Interview Process

Stage 1: Introductory Call (45 minutes)

An introductory conversation covering your professional background and what you’re looking for in your next role.

Stage 2: Hiring Manager Call (30 minutes)

A conversation with Marcus focused on ways of working and team collaboration.

Stage 3: Technical Deep Dive (60 minutes)

An in-depth discussion exploring your architectural thinking and past technical decisions.

Stage 4: Leadership Scenario Interview (60 minutes)

An onsite interview at our London office, where we’ll walk through real challenges you’d likely face in the role.

Final Stage: Founders Interview

A conversation with our co-founders, Anders and Marcus, focused on values alignment and long-term vision.

Upon mutual fit: references and offer stage.

title: Engineering Manager - Unified Platform
descriptionHtml:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

About the Team

The Unified Privacy Platform team's mission is to earn the trust of every DoorDash user by upholding their right to privacy, consent, and transparency. We are building a common privacy foundation across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo so Consumers, Dashers, and Merchants can understand how their data is used, control their choices, and exercise their privacy rights through simple, consistent experiences.

Our work is organized around three connected pillars: the Privacy Center, a unified user-facing destination for privacy controls and rights; the Unified Privacy Platform, which captures and enforces consent, policy, jurisdictional requirements, and privacy actions; and Privacy Operations and Intelligence, which gives Legal, Support, Privacy, and engineering operators the workflows, diagnostics, audit history, and automation needed to resolve privacy work safely and efficiently.

Together, these capabilities turn fragmented, one-off compliance work into reusable platform primitives that can support new products, brands, and emerging regulations.

Location: London, UK. This is a hybrid role, with 3 days a week in the office.

About the Role

DoorDash is looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the Unified Privacy Platform team. You will lead a team of backend and platform engineers responsible for the next generation of privacy and consent infrastructure, including the Privacy Center, the User Consent Platform, privacy-policy decisioning, self-service data-rights experiences, and the operational tooling required to manage privacy cases at global scale.

As the Engineering Manager, you will own and execute a multi-year vision for privacy at DoorDash. You will balance legal and regulatory correctness, user trust, security, reliability, and developer velocity while building systems that work consistently across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. You will be a strategic partner to Product, Legal, Security, Data Governance, Marketing and Communications, and engineering leadership, establishing clear ownership boundaries and turning complex privacy requirements into scalable, self-service capabilities.

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

  • Lead and mentor a high-performing team of backend and platform engineers, fostering a culture of ownership, privacy by design, operational excellence, and thoughtful cross-functional partnership
  • Drive the technical strategy across the Privacy Center, the Unified Privacy Platform, and Privacy Operations and Intelligence
  • Build the cross-brand User Consent Platform, including canonical consent state, policy and configuration management, consent SDKs, audit history, and consistent enforcement across products and jurisdictions
  • Deliver simple, self-service experiences for consent and communication preferences, Right to be Forgotten (RTF), Right to Information (RTI), and Data Subject Access Requests (DSARs)
  • Turn emerging privacy and regulatory requirements into standardized platform capabilities instead of one-off product implementations
  • Lead the migration from fragmented legacy consent systems to a single source of truth across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo, while managing compatibility and safe deprecation
  • Define clear contracts with data-governance fulfillment systems and downstream product and storage teams so privacy actions are traceable, retryable, auditable, and correctly reflected back to users and operators
  • Provide architectural guidance for distributed systems that manage sensitive user choices, policy evaluation, orchestration, secure data delivery, reporting, and immutable audit trails
  • Partner with recruiting to build a diverse and inclusive team, attracting and retaining exceptional engineering talent

We're excited about you because you have…

  • A bachelor's, master's, or doctoral degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

title: Event Management (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Deine Rolle

Mittelständische Unternehmer erleben Beratungen meist in einer austauschbaren Eventsprache: Konferenzhotel, Standard-Catering, ein Programm, das in jedem Raum gleich aussieht. Genau dort liegt der Hebel für ein anderes Modell, über alle Anlassgrößen vom Webinar bis zur eigenen Konferenz.

Vogel berät mehrere Tausend mittelständische Unternehmen in steuerlichen, kaufmännischen und strategischen Fragen. Für dieses Netzwerk bauen wir die Event-Infrastruktur auf: Roundtables, Retreats, Salon-Formate, individuelle Mandanten-Dinner, eine laufende Webinar-Reihe, ausgewählte Messeauftritte und perspektivisch eine eigene Mittelstandskonferenz. Auch unsere internen Anlässe wie Town Hall, Sommerfest und Off-sites sollen sich anfühlen wie Vogel und nicht wie ein Standard-Firmenfest.

Du kommst aus der Premium-Hospitality, aus einem gehobenen Restaurant oder von einer Event-Marke mit hohem Anspruch und willst Formate selbst entwerfen, statt fertige Konzepte umzusetzen. Du verantwortest die Event- und Brand-Experience von Vogel, arbeitest im Growth-Team und eng mit der Geschäftsführung an ausgewählten Formaten. Nach 24 bis 36 Monaten führt der natürliche Weg in eine Lead-Rolle für Event und Brand Experience.

Deine Verantwortung

Flagship-Anlässe und individuelle Formate

  • Du entwirfst die Format-Bibliothek von Vogel, vom Salon über das kuratierte Dinner bis zum Retreat, und trägst jeden Anlass vom Konzept bis zum letzten Detail.

  • Du baust die eigene Mittelstandskonferenz mit auf: Bühne, Programm, Catering, Eingangserlebnis.

  • Du verantwortest Formate im kleinen Kreis: Mandanten-Dinner nach Branche, persönliche Termine mit Multiplikatoren, Salons mit wenigen Gästen.

Laufender Betrieb: Webinare, interne Anlässe, Messen

  • Du koordinierst die Webinar-Reihe mit zwei bis drei Terminen pro Woche: Technik, Ablaufplan, Nachbereitung und Nachverfolgung im CRM. Die Berater halten die Inhalte, du hältst den Standard.

  • Du verantwortest den Rahmen unserer internen Anlässe auf demselben Detail-Standard wie nach außen.

  • Du steuerst unsere Präsenz auf ausgewählten Messen, vom Standkonzept bis zum Auftritt vor Ort.

Markenstandard und Abläufe

  • Du hältst jeden Anlass gegen unser Stylebook: warme Tischkultur, reduzierte Gestaltung, echte Materialien.

  • Du pflegst die Gästelisten mit der Geschäftsführung und dem Business Development: kuratiert, nicht im Massenversand.

  • Du dokumentierst wiederverwendbare Standards, vom Eingangsritual bis zum Webinar-Ablauf, damit sie ohne dich tragen.

Deine Perspektiven

Was du nach 6 Monaten geliefert hast:

  • Du hast die ersten Roundtables und Retreats eigenständig getragen und parallel die Webinar-Reihe übernommen.

  • Du hast eine eigene Format-Bibliothek aufgebaut: Flagship-Formate, Webinar-Ablauf, Playbook für interne Anlässe.

Was du nach 12 Monaten geliefert hast:

  • Du trägst fünfzehn bis zwanzig Flagship-Anlässe im Jahr und die laufende Webinar-Reihe eigenständig.

  • Die internen Anlässe laufen auf demselben Standard wie die Formate für Mandanten.

Was du nach 24 Monaten geliefert hast:

  • Die eigene Mittelstandskonferenz ist gelaufen und hat einen Ruf über unsere Mandanten hinaus.

  • Du bist Kandidat für die Lead-Rolle Event und Brand Experience.

Wohin sich die Stelle entwickelt:

Der nächste Schritt ist die Lead-Rolle für Event und Brand Experience. Sie setzt eine eigenständig getragene Event-Architektur und sichtbare Format-Reputation voraus, nicht zusätzliche Berufsjahre.

Das bringst du mit

Erfahrung & Track Record

  • Belegbare Praxis in der Premium-Hospitality: in einer Hotelmarke mit hohem Service-Anspruch, einem gehobenen Restaurant oder bei einer Event-Marke für anspruchsvolle Gäste.

  • Du hast neben Flagship-Anlässen auch den laufenden Betrieb in hoher Frequenz verantwortet, mit demselben Detail-Standard.

  • Profile, die nicht in dieses Raster passen, aber Format-Gespür und Sinn für Details mitbringen, sind ausdrücklich eingeladen. Konkret: Innenarchitekten mit Praxis im Eventbau, Producer aus Magazinen mit Live-Formaten, Quereinsteiger aus Theater oder Oper. Wir bewerten am Beitrag, nicht am Etikett. Die ausgewiesene Spanne ist kein Verhandlungsspielraum, sondern eine Profil-Skala: Das untere Ende steht für belegbare Praxis in der Premium-Hospitality, das obere Ende für eigene Format-Architektur und einen erkennbaren Methodenbeitrag. Wer einen anderen Hintergrund mitbringt, startet zu einem anderen Marktpreis und konvergiert nach zwölf Monaten bewährter Leistung auf das Rollen-Niveau.

Skills & Arbeitsweise

  • Du hast Gespür für Details: Im Catering-Briefing, im Lichtkonzept oder in der Bestuhlung erkennst du, was trägt und was kippt.

  • Du beherrschst Webinar-Werkzeuge und Ablaufplanung und löst operative Engpässe selbst, statt sie zu eskalieren.

  • Du arbeitest mit KI als selbstverständlichem Werkzeug für Recherche, Einladungstexte und Ablaufpläne.

Mindset & Persönlichkeit

  • Du hast den Anspruch, in allem, was du ablieferst, den höchsten Standard zu setzen, nicht weil jemand es kontrolliert, sondern weil Mittelmaß dich persönlich stört.

  • Du bringst die Demut mit, von Praktikern zu lernen. Mandanten und Berater wissen Dinge über den Mittelstand, die in keinem Hospitality-Handbuch stehen.

  • Du fühlst dich wohl in einer Kultur, die hierarchisch in der Entscheidung, flach in der Kommunikation und autonom in der Ausführung ist.

Was du bei uns nicht finden wirst

  • Keinen Event-Job mit ausgelagerter Logistik. Du machst Konzept und Umsetzung zugleich.

  • Kein reines Webinar-Marketing. Du verantwortest das ganze Erlebnis über alle Anlassgrößen.

  • Keinen Agentur-Hochglanz. Wir arbeiten in kurzen Zyklen, in kleinen Teams und schrauben selbst am Detail.

  • Keinen Aufstieg über Personalspanne. Du wächst über fachliche Tiefe.

FAQ

1. Was ist Vogel – und wo arbeitet ihr?

Vogel ist eine der führenden Mittelstandsberatungen Deutschlands – seit 1959, inhabergeführt in zweiter Generation, mit eigenem Kapital – und baut daraus die führende Beratungsplattform für den Mittelstand. Wir arbeiten an drei Standorten: Aalen als gewachsenem Stammsitz, Bopfingen im Kerngeschäft und München als neuem Hub. An allen dreien suchen wir quer durch die Funktionen – von Steuerberatung über Beratung bis zu den Teams, die das Fundament darunter bauen.

2. Wie sind die Gehaltsbänder zu verstehen?

Bewusst breit – und an jeder Stelle ausgewiesen, bevor du dich bewirbst. Wir differenzieren nach Track Record und Marktwert, nicht nach Abschluss: knappe, stark gefragte Profile am oberen Ende, weniger knappe am unteren. Die ausgewiesene Spanne ist kein Verhandlungsspielraum, sondern eine Profil-Skala – zwei Menschen mit ähnlicher Erfahrung können bei uns unterschiedlich verdienen. Was das obere Ende bestimmt, ist der Reifegrad, nicht die Zahl der Berufsjahre und nicht das Verhandlungsgeschick.

3. Wie viel – und wie – wird bei Vogel gearbeitet?

Gemessen wird an dem, was du bewegst, nicht an Stunden. Ehrlich ist aber auch: Wer 9-to-5 sucht, ist bei uns nicht die erste Adresse. Wir suchen Menschen, die aus eigenem Antrieb intensiv arbeiten, weil die Aufgaben es wert sind. Wie du deine Zeit verteilst, ist weitgehend deine Sache. Was wir teilen: Wir arbeiten präsent zusammen und sehen uns im Normalfall täglich im Büro – Kultur, Sparring und die besten Ideen entstehen in der täglichen Nähe. Wir sind keine Remote-Company und haben keine großen Home-Office-Policies; einzelne Remote-Tage sind kein Problem.

4. Wie läuft die Bewerbung?

Schlank, schnell, transparent – und nach Profil gestaffelt. In der Regel sind es vier Schritte: eine schriftliche Aufgabe, in der du zu acht Fragen Position beziehst – KI ist ausdrücklich erlaubt, wir bitten nur um eine kurze Selbstauskunft dazu; ein Gespräch von einer halben Stunde; eine gemeinsame Arbeitssitzung an einem echten Problem aus unserem Alltag; und ein Termin vor Ort mit dem Team und gemeinsamem Essen. Wie viele Schritte es tatsächlich werden, hängt von der Rolle ab: Bei Praktikum und Werkstudium fällt der Vor-Ort-Termin weg, für Schülerjobs genügt ein Gespräch, bei Senior-Rollen kommt ein gemeinsamer Arbeitsnachmittag dazu. Vorab kannst du einen Zehn-Minuten-Call buchen, in dem nur du fragst. In der Regel hörst du nach jedem Schritt innerhalb von 48 Stunden von uns.

5. Wie funktioniert die variable Vergütung?

Quartalsweise an Leistung gekoppelt, qualitativ bewertet. Die Skala steigt mit dem Level: bis 20 % Associate, 27,5 % Manager, 35 % Senior Manager, 42,5 % Director, 50 % VP. Erwartungswert bei guter Leistung – du erfüllst die Anforderungen, setzt eigene Akzente, bestehst den Keeper Test – liegt bei rund 50 % des Maximums; der Maximalbonus ist nicht der Normalfall. Im Fokus steht eine ganzheitliche Beurteilung durch deine Führungskraft anhand von sechs Kriterien: Impact, Judgement, Communication, Execution, Growth und Values.

6. Wie entwickle ich mich – welche Karrierewege gibt es?

Zwei aktive Wege: die IC-Karriere (fachliche Tiefe, Expertenlaufbahn) über die Stufen Expert, Senior, Lead und Principal – und die Management-Karriere (Führung, Personalverantwortung) über Manager, Senior Manager, Director und VP. Beide werden gleich vergütet, und beide müssen nicht nach oben führen: Wer auf einer Stufe bleibt und dort weiter in die Tiefe geht, ist bei uns genauso richtig. Die Richtung wählst du nach dem Onboarding, meist in Jahr 1–3. Berufseinstieg ist kein Sonderweg, sondern der frühe Teil derselben Strecke – vom Werkstudenten oder Praktikanten zum Associate, für die Besten ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren.

7. Team, Kultur, Urlaub?

Das gemeinsame Mittagessen ist der tägliche Ankerpunkt – wer im Büro ist, isst mit; erwartet, nicht kontrolliert. Das Abendessen ist dasselbe Angebot ohne jede Erwartung. Beides ohne Eigenanteil. Dazu Social Events und Offsites in regelmäßigem Rhythmus – nicht als Pflichtprogramm, sondern weil ein gutes Team auch abseits der Arbeit Zeit teilt.

Benefits sind bei uns nicht das Sahnehäubchen, sondern das, was Intensität über Jahre tragbar macht: Examensförderung mit 25.000 EUR Qualifizierungsbudget und drei Monaten Freistellung, 100-prozentige Übernahme der Kinderbetreuung, EGYM Wellpass, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Job-Ticket mit 90 % Zuschuss, Homeoffice-Ausstattung und ein Gerät deiner Wahl aus unserem Katalog, ein Buch im Monat aus dem Vogel-Kanon – und KI-Tools ohne Token-Limit und ohne Budgetdeckel. Urlaub: 28 Tage.

Rejoins Pennylane en tant qu’Expert·e Support Technique et Comptable.

Tu prends en charge les sujets les plus complexes remontés par nos utilisateurs et nos équipes Support.
Ton objectif : comprendre l’origine des problèmes, qu’ils soient comptables, fonctionnels ou techniques, puis coordonner leur résolution avec les équipes Produit et Tech.

About Isembard

Isembard is building a network of high-performance factories for critical industries. We combine advanced machine tools, robotics and our own software, MasonOS, to make precision components for aerospace, defence, energy and frontier technology companies, with factories across the UK, US, Germany and France. Our mission is to forge industrial acceleration.

The role

Isembard makes precision parts for aerospace and defence customers from factories across the UK, US, Germany and France. Goods, software and technical data move between our sites, suppliers and customers, and each transfer has to comply with UK, EU, US and other export-control and sanctions regimes.

The Export Control Officer runs the programme that makes this work and makes sure the people doing the work know what to do. This is our first dedicated export-control hire. The focus is the UK first, with France, Germany and the US to follow, and there is scope to lead the function as it grows.

What you'll do

  • Run and improve the export-control compliance programme, policies and procedures.

  • Act as the principal point of contact on export control internally and with regulators and customers.

  • Classify goods, software and technical data against the relevant control lists, and keep central records so repeat orders do not need reassessing.

  • Prepare and manage export licences and authorisations, including their conditions and reporting.

  • Operate technology control plans and access controls for controlled technical data.

What we're looking for

  • Experience running an export-control programme in a defence, aerospace or advanced-manufacturing environment.

  • Hands-on UK export licensing experience (SPIRE / LITE) and confident use of the UK military and dual-use lists.

  • Working knowledge of EU dual-use controls, the US ITAR and EAR, and UK, EU and US sanctions regimes.

  • An understanding of deemed-export principles and access controls for foreign persons.

  • Accuracy and attention to detail in classification and record-keeping.

Nice to have

  • Hands-on ITAR experience, including managing TAAs and MLAs.

  • Experience building an export-control function from scratch.

  • Professional export-control certification. We value experience over formal qualifications.

Why Isembard

  • Own a function at an early stage and shape how it works.

  • Work closely with engineering, operations, IT security and leadership in a growing manufacturing business.

Location: On-site at our Southwark site in London, with travel to company and customer sites.

Eligibility: This role may require eligibility to access controlled technical data, which can depend on nationality, residency, security-clearance or licensing conditions. The successful candidate must pass pre-employment screening and any applicable export-control or security-clearance requirements.

title: Fabrication Technician (Cleanroom) (Contract)
descriptionHtml:
About OLIX

AI is growing faster than any technology in history and the explosion in demand has created a massive infrastructure gap; we can no longer build chips or power stations fast enough to keep up. The industry is still leaning on a ten-year-old hardware blueprint that has reached its limit. A new paradigm that is faster and more efficient will be the biggest economic opportunity of the next century and create the most important company of the next decade. The OLIX Decode Accelerator 1 (DX-1) is the first accelerator architected specifically for decode. Rack-scale co-design of logic, data movement, packaging, optics and interconnect enables a step change in system level performance.


About the role

This is a chance to get hands-on at the heart of a fast-growing AI hardware company. You'll run a micro-fabrication process flow in our London cleanroom, and the samples you make go straight into the prototypes our engineers are building for the next generation of AI infrastructure.

This role suits someone with excellent cleanroom discipline who takes pride in careful, repeatable work and wants to see it make a difference fast.


This is a 3-6 month contract role.


What you'll do

  • You'll run established process steps from written procedures, working closely with our process engineers

  • Run cleanroom process steps such as substrate preparation and photolithography, following SOPs exactly

  • Operate and look after process tools: routine checks, simple maintenance and flagging faults early

  • Inspect work in progress for defects using metrology tools and decide when to stop and escalate

  • Take routine measurements, such as thickness, surface profile and feature dimensions, to set methods

  • Prepare samples for test and hand them over to the engineering team.

  • Keep accurate run records so every sample is traceable

  • Keep the cleanroom running: gowning discipline, housekeeping, consumables, materials storage and safe chemical handling

  • Support engineers on experiments and report clearly what you observed


What you'll bring

  • Excellent cleanroom practice is the core requirement; we'll train you on our specific tools and recipes

  • At least one year of hands-on work in a cleanroom (ISO 7 or better), in industry or as a regular research cleanroom user

  • Practical fabrication experience: demonstrated ability to independently operate fabrication processes and record measurement results using metrology tools

  • Excellent contamination control: full-gowning, clean handling and working steadily in a cleanroom for long sessions

  • Careful defect inspection under a microscope, and the judgement to stop and flag a problem

  • Meticulous record-keeping: you follow SOPs exactly and write down what actually happened

  • Safe working with chemicals, hot equipment, UV light and lasers

  • Right to work in the UK, and eligibility under the export-control conditions below


Nice to have

  • Experience across several process areas, such as coating, bonding, wet processing, deposition or etch

  • Metrology: stylus or optical profilometry, confocal microscopy and thickness measurement

  • Work in a production or pilot-line setting (semiconductor, MEMS, PCB, display or medical devices) as well as in R&D

  • A degree, or study towards one, in physics, materials science, chemistry or engineering

  • Simple data handling in Excel or Python for run logs and SPC charts


Due to U.S. export control regulations, candidates’ eligibility to work at OLIX depends on their most recent citizenship or permanent residency status. We are generally unable to consider applicants whose most recent citizenship or permanent residence is in certain restricted countries (currently including Iran, North Korea, Syria, Cuba, Russia, Belarus, China, Hong Kong, Macau, and Venezuela). Applicants who have subsequently obtained citizenship or permanent residency in another country not subject to these restrictions may still be eligible.

title: Field CTO, London
descriptionHtml:
Location: London, UK

Travel: Frequent travel across EMEA required

ABOUT WEKA

WEKA is architecting a new approach to the enterprise data stack, built for the AI era. The WEKA Data Platform sets the standard for AI infrastructure with a cloud and AI-native software solution that can be deployed anywhere. It transforms legacy data silos into data pipelines that make GPUs, AI, and other performance-intensive workloads run faster, work more efficiently, and consume less energy.

WEKA is a pre-IPO, growth-stage company on a hyper-growth trajectory. We've raised $375M in capital from dozens of world-class venture capital and strategic investors. We help the world's most innovative enterprises and research organizations (including 12 of the Fortune 50), reach discoveries, insights, and outcomes faster and more sustainably.

We're passionate about helping our customers overcome complex data challenges to accelerate their innovation and grow their businesses. If you share our passion, we would love for you to join us on this exciting journey.

WHAT'S COOL ABOUT THIS JOB

As WEKA's Field CTO for EDA and AI, based in London and covering the broader EMEA region, you'll sit at the intersection of two of the most demanding compute domains in the industry: semiconductor design (EDA) and AI infrastructure. You'll work directly with chip designers, foundries, and AI teams across EMEA to architect solutions on the WEKA Data Platform, investigate new innovations across both fields, and champion WEKA as the platform of choice for design and AI workloads. You'll collaborate with the wider CTO Office to translate customer requirements into solutions and architectures, and act as the region's technical evangelist for WEKA in EDA and AI.

RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE

  • Connect WEKA's EDA and AI customers across EMEA to the broader WEKA team, alongside other members of the CTO Office.
  • Partner with the GTM team to develop and deliver compelling technical presentations, demonstrations, and customer workshops that showcase WEKA's value proposition in semiconductor design and AI workloads.
  • Act as a trusted advisor to GTM teams and customers, providing deep technical expertise on how WEKA's technology solves EDA and AI-specific technical and business challenges.
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders across product, engineering, and marketing to align customer needs, technology strategy, and product roadmap.
  • Deliver advisory services to the field, working with WEKA's presales and post-sales organizations to drive successful outcomes on both types of engagements.
  • Provide oversight on large, complex EDA and AI customer engagements across the region where appropriate.
  • Champion technical innovation across functions inside and outside GTM, staying current on emerging EDA and AI technologies and assessing their impact on the business.
  • Cultivate partnerships with technology providers (EDA vendors, foundries, hyperscalers, GPU vendors) to address customer requirements and expand WEKA's reach and influence across EMEA.
  • Represent WEKA at industry events, conferences, and workshops across the region, establishing thought leadership in EDA and AI infrastructure.
  • Identify emerging market trends and technologies across EDA and AI to inform product development and go-to-market strategy.

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 15+ years of technical experience in relevant industries
  • Proven experience architecting AI infrastructure environments; hands-on experience with EDA (Electronic Design Automation) workflows and semiconductor design compute environments.
  • Proven track record deploying and utilizing multiple AI frameworks and technologies.
  • Excellent English communication and presentation skills, with the ability to engage both technical and non-technical audiences across a diverse regional customer base.
  • Demonstrated experience and proven skills as a technical evangelist, including designing and running customer workshops.
  • Comfortable with frequent travel across EMEA.
  • Ability to translate technical terms into business value for varied audiences, specifically across traditional enterprises adopting AI, foundational model builders, neocloud providers and semiconductor design houses. 
  • Experience building and maintaining strong relationships with customers and partners.
  • A collaborative, results-oriented mindset with a strong work ethic and genuine passion for staying ahead of the technology curve.

Concerned you don't meet every qualification? Don't let it stop you from applying.

title: Financial Administrator
descriptionHtml:
Hi, I'm Alex, Finance Manager at FeedbackFruits. 👋

Our Finance team is ramping up over the next couple of years, and we are looking for someone to join the team on a 24-32 hour basis! Finance here runs across two entities, a Dutch BV and a US Corp, each with its own invoicing, tax and banking rules. Our customers are universities all over the world, so the work ranges from a straightforward Dutch invoice to a US procurement portal with its own supplier onboarding forms and submission rules. The role is broader than most financial administration jobs at this level, and we are searching for someone who's ready to own it.

I'm looking for a Financial Administrator to take on our day-to-day operations: billing and collections on the receivables side, supplier invoices and payment runs on the payables side, and the Finance mailbox where everything is coordinated. A lot of our processes are still manual, with limited documented processes. You'd be doing the work and improving it at the same time, formalising operating procedures as you go. The ideal team member is someone who notices when a workflow is clumsy, and is proactive in addressing it.

We're a small team of two, and we support the wider organisation with a vast range of topics. You'd work closely with our New Business and Partner Success teams when it comes to billing, and with our Marketing team when it comes to purchasing. When an invoice goes out on time, a university pays on schedule or a purchasing inquiry is resolved ahead of an event, that's visible, and it will be thanks to you. Financial administration can often be limited to a narrow scope of topics within a larger team. If you're eager to get the full picture of operations in a company with an international customer base, this is the right place for it.

What you'll do:

  • Send out sales invoices on time. This includes setting up new customers and uploading invoices to procurement portals such as Ariba and PaymentWorks

  • Set up and maintain customer subscriptions in the ERP system based on signed contracts, and create invoices and credit notes for all legal entities

  • Keep track of unpaid invoices, send payment reminders to institutions that haven’t paid, and flag invoices that stay unpaid

  • Partner with Sales and Partner Success to address billing and payment queries

What you bring:

You will blend deep process and industry expertise with a proven consulting skill set with strong analytical skills at the forefront of one of the fastest-growing tech companies worldwide.

Native-level German proficiency is required for this role. Candidates must be able to lead customer workshops, conduct executive presentations, and manage stakeholder interactions in German.

The role is based in Munich.

Identify & Frame Value

Realize Value

Data, Analytics, Applications & IT: Good knowledge of Business Software / SaaS applications (e.g. SAP),  experience with implementing RPA and/or BI Tools and/or building Dashboards, Apps and Action Flows. Knowledge of Python and/or SQL. Experience in collaborating with IT teams.

Process Improvement & Value Realization: Experience in identifying use cases for business process improvement and deploying improvement measures,  being a change agent and training users/process owners to realize value

Project Management: Experience in planning and managing project scopes, expectations and timelines. You will manage multiple projects across your aligned accounts that will be at different parts of the value journey. Also, you will leverage partners from the Celonis Ecosystem wherever possible.

Executive Stakeholder Management: Experience in preparing and communicating (value) roadmaps and results to stakeholders and management, both internally and externally. Excellent communication and presentation skills.

Industry Expertise: Ideally expertise in one or more industries (e.g. Manufacturing, Automotive, Consumer, Retail, Pharmaceuticals, Chemicals) and the ability to develop a deep understanding of industry trends and strategic opportunities 

Degree: In Technology & Management, Industrial/Business Engineering, Business Informatics, Computer Science, Mathematics, Economics or a comparable degree program

Native-level or near-native German language skills (written and spoken), with the ability to confidently engage German-speaking customers, facilitate workshops, and present to executive stakeholders.
