title: Partner Solutions Architect
descriptionHtml:
Retire the ERP

Light exists to replace factory-era ERPs with software that feels alive. Our Smart Financial Platform gives modern, global companies superpowers - automated accounting, real-time reporting, and financial flows that move at the speed of the business.

We build with our customers, ship fast, and obsess over craft. In a short time, Light has gone from idea to the operating core for leading companies like Lovable, Legora, and Fuse Energy.

We're an early team defining a new software category. Think engineers who love debits and credits, designers who care about reconciliation states, and operators who treat finance as a product. If you're excited to modernise how companies run money, you're in the right place.

Backed by world-class investors including Balderton and Atomico and advised by industry titans, we're building category-defining products with the freedom to ship ambitiously and own outcomes. Come help us make Light the global default for next-gen finance.

About the role

Light doesn't implement Light alone anymore. Accounting and consulting firms, from regional champions to global names, are building Light implementation practices. Someone has to make sure those practices deliver to Light's standard on every deal. That's you.

You'll be one of the first Partner Solutions Architects at Light, sitting between our partners, their clients and our own implementation team. Most of your week goes on running a portfolio of partner-led implementations. You know which deals are on track and which are drifting. You know whether each partner has the people and capacity to take on the next one, and you're the person Light goes to for an answer on any partner deal. You also get new partner consultants trained and certified. When a partner hits something new, hard, or beyond their capacity, you step in and do the work yourself.

This is not a training role. We want a consultant with commercial instincts, someone who has delivered finance implementations, can hold their own with a Financial Controller, and can manage a book of delivery the way a good account manager manages a book of revenue. Your audience is partner implementation teams, the leaders who run them, and their clients' Controllers, Finance Directors and CFOs. They're senior, technical and short on time, and they expect you to tell them straight when something won't work.

Key responsibilities

Own partner delivery across your portfolio

  • Check every deal through Light's delivery gates: did the partner get through it, on time, to the right standard?

  • Run weekly check-ins with each partner on progress, blockers, risks and upcoming go-lives

  • Track partner capacity and staffing: who they have, who's certified, what they can take on next, and when

  • Build and own the partner delivery forecast so Sales can always tell a customer yes, with a start date we can stand behind

  • Represent Light on partner deals from day one: run kickoffs with the partner and client, and drive data collection until the partner team is ready to take over

  • Spot deliveries going off track before the client does, and intervene

  • Report clearly to Light leadership on partner delivery health, capacity and quality, so nobody ever has to ask "who owns this deal?"

Get partner teams trained and certified

  • Bring new partner consultants through Light's enablement path, from self-paced curriculum and instructor-led sessions through to certification

  • Schedule the training, track progress and hold the certification bar firm

  • Teach clearly, whether the room holds a partner associate or a client CFO

  • Feed what you learn on live deals back into the curriculum, the playbooks and the product

Step in as the expert when partners can't

  • Take on consulting work directly when a partner meets something new or complex, or runs out of capacity: a consolidation edge case, an unusual migration, a tricky entity structure

  • Coach partners on turning finance requirements into platform design: chart of accounts, entity structure, consolidation logic, reporting

  • Know Light well enough to demo any workflow credibly and answer the hard configuration and accounting questions partners bring you

Experience & qualifications

  • Degree in finance, accounting, business, or a related field

  • 5+ years in finance transformation, ERP implementation or finance advisory: Big 4, a finance-focused boutique, or a vendor-side professional services team (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Workday Financials)

  • You've done the work: hands-on roles on real implementations, not "I've used an ERP"

  • You're fluent in accounting and can hold your own with a Controller on multi-entity consolidation, intercompany eliminations, accruals, and statutory vs management reporting. A qualified accountant is a plus, not a requirement

  • You've managed a portfolio, not just a project: many moving deals, many stakeholders, one clear view of where everything stands

  • Commercial or client-facing experience beyond delivery is a strong signal, for example account management, client services, or a pre-sales or sales role

  • You're highly organised and analytical. You like a good forecast, keep clean data, and spot the deal that's quietly going wrong

  • You're a strong communicator and a confident presenter, and you've trained or coached other consultants at some point in your career

  • You work well through people who don't report to you, and build trust with partner leadership and client finance teams through clear communication and consistent follow-through

  • You use AI tools daily, and have specific opinions on where they help in delivery work and where they don't

  • Fluent English; additional European languages a plus, German especially

  • Bonus: a go-live with your name on it as the accountable lead; multi-jurisdiction experience (IFRS, US GAAP, local GAAPs); experience at or with an implementation partner; experience losing a customer or missing a go-live and learning from it

The good stuff

In addition to being part of a great team and working in a really fun and innovative environment, we offer:

💸 A competitive salary + potential stock options

🏝 Generous package of paid annual leave + public holidays

🥳 Regular socials and company off-sites (last time was in Piemonte, next time is in Provence)

🚀 A huge opportunity for career growth as you'll help shape a market-defining motion

The famous last words

Working at Light means you're embarking on an exciting journey to reshape the future of multinational financial operations. Our cheat-code is that we've built something like this before - and are now doing it again, only better. Our goal is to make global finance effortless and empower companies to make informed decisions.

Join the rocket ship while it's taking off 🚀

title: Partnerships Manager - M&A Platform
descriptionHtml:
The company

It's still difficult for business owners to sell their business, or buy others, in the sub-£10m enterprise value market. Information asymmetry, lack of knowledge and low transaction values make it hard, and most M&A firms shy away from the segment because they can't serve it profitably. A generation of owner-managers is approaching retirement, and most of them have no realistic route to a sale.

manda exists to fix that. We match buyers with sellers in the part of the market everyone else ignores, and we finance acquisitions ourselves so buyers arrive pre-qualified and often pre-financed. We've sold the first businesses, funded the first acquisition loans, and we're now opening the platform up beyond the businesses that already bank with us.

manda is part of iwoca, one of Europe's leading fintech lenders. Since 2012 iwoca has provided more than £4 billion in funding and its mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments. That backing is why we can serve this market where others can't: a deep footprint in the SME economy with 150,000+ UK customers, the data and infrastructure of an established lender, and the ability to build clean, automated processes instead of running an advisory firm on spreadsheets.

We’re looking for a Partnership Manager - manda (iwoca's M&A Platform)

We're looking for someone to build the introducer network that brings business owners to manda, iwoca's M&A platform. Accountants, solicitors, wealth managers and brokers meet an owner who is thinking about retiring long before we do. Your job is to make sure that when they do they think of us, and that referring us is the easiest thing they do that day.

The role

Your mission is to build a referral channel that produces a steady flow of business owners who are genuinely ready to sell.

Today almost all of our sellers come from iwoca's own customer base, found by hand and worked one at a time. That works, but the pool is finite. The professionals who already advise business owners are the most credible route to the ones we'd otherwise never reach, and right now we have no systematic way of working with them.

You'll be starting from close to nothing, so the first version of this channel is yours to design. It also means the job is as much about making referrals actually arrive as it is about signing partners up.

It also has to scale. In this industry most partner flow still depends on people turning up at industry events, which works but stops the moment you stop showing up. We're after the version of this channel where referring a client to manda takes a couple of clicks inside the software an adviser already uses.

Key responsibilities include:

Build the introducer network

  • Find and win the firms worth working with: accountancy practices, corporate finance boutiques, solicitors, wealth managers and business transfer agents. Work out which kinds of firm actually refer, and concentrate there.

  • Do the outbound yourself. Identify the firm, get the meeting, make the case, and follow up until something happens.

  • Design what we offer them: how a referral is made, what the partner gets, what we commit to in return, and how we keep them informed once their client is with us.

Make referrals actually arrive

  • A signed partnership is worth nothing until a referral comes through. You'll own the ongoing relationship work that turns agreements into a flow: regular contact, keeping manda front of mind, briefing partner teams, and being the person they call.

  • Track referral volume and quality by partner, and be honest about which relationships aren't working so we can stop spending time on them.

Make the channel scale

  • Judge every partnership by whether it adds referrals without adding work. A relationship that only produces when you're in the room isn't a channel yet.

  • Work out which partner technology is worth plugging into: the practice management and accounting software advisers already work in, tracked referral links and partner portals, and integrations that let a firm refer a client without leaving their own tools. You won't build these yourself, but you'll identify them, make the commercial case, and scope them with our Product Builder.

  • Look for partners who can bring a book rather than one client at a time. One firm with hundreds of owner-managed clients is worth more to us than ten firms with five, if we can find a way to surface the right candidates across the whole book.

Work iwoca's existing network

  • iwoca already has a broker network and a partnerships function with relationships across the SME economy. Working out where manda fits into those relationships is far faster than starting cold, and it's the first place to look.

Events and community

  • Build a focused programme of events worth attending and, where it makes sense, running our own: succession and exit planning, accountancy and adviser events, industry gatherings, and business owner peer communities.

  • Judge them on referrals rather than attendance, and stop going to the ones that don't produce. Events are how you find and land partners, not how the channel scales.

Prove the channel pays

  • Establish what a referral actually costs us once your time, any partner incentives and events are counted, and how many convert into a signed mandate. We have an assumption in our financial model and nobody has yet tested it.

The requirements

We look for people who are smart, humble, motivated and who are always looking to improve.

Essential:

  • Around 4+ years in partnerships, channel or business development, ideally B2B, where you built or substantially grew a referral channel rather than inheriting one that already worked.

  • You've done the full cycle yourself: identified the target firms, got the meetings, agreed the terms, and then managed the relationship afterwards.

  • A background in M&A, marketplaces, business broking or business transfer.

  • You understand that the work starts after the agreement is signed, and you have the discipline to keep a channel warm over months rather than weeks.

  • Numerate and honest about performance. You track referrals by partner, you know which relationships are producing, and you say so when one isn't.

  • You think in systems as well as relationships. You can tell the difference between a partnership that scales and one that only works while you're pushing it, and you'd rather replace your own manual work with an integration than defend it.

  • Comfortable specifying technology without building it. You can look at a partner's tools and our product, work out what would make us the path of least resistance, and scope it clearly enough for a product team to build.

  • Genuinely hands-on. There's no team to delegate to: you'll build the target list, send the emails, run the meetings and keep the CRM straight yourself.

  • A commercial thinker with a bias for action, comfortable navigating ambiguity in an early-stage venture.

Bonus:

  • Experience with accountancy, legal or wealth management channels specifically.

  • Experience running an event programme with commercial targets attached to it.

  • Familiarity with the UK succession and exit planning landscape.

  • Comfortable treating a CRM as a discipline rather than an afterthought, ideally HubSpot.

  • You've shipped a partner integration, an embedded referral flow or a software marketplace listing, or worked closely with a product team on one.

  • Familiar with the software UK accountancy practices and advisers actually work in, such as Xero, QuickBooks, Sage, IRIS or Dext.

The salary

We expect to pay £55,000–£80,000 and an annual performance based bonus for this role. But, we're open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

PlantaCorp ist ein ISO 22000- und GMP-zertifizierter deutscher Hersteller von liposomalen Nahrungsergänzungsmitteln. Unsere einzigartige, fortschrittliche Technologie zur Verkapselung von Vitalstoffen versorgt unsere Kunden mit hoch-effektiven, maximal absorbierbaren liposomalen Nahrungsergänzungsmitteln. Unsere 1.500 m² große, hochmoderne Produktionsstätte sowie unsere Büroräumlichkeiten befinden sich in Eidelstedt, Hamburg.

Wir als PlantaCorp unterstützen unsere Geschäftspartner bei der Eroberung des globalen Marktes sowohl mit unserer Auftragsherstellung als auch mit unseren White-Labelling-Services. Gemeinsam gestalten wir die Zukunft, indem wir eine neue Sichtweise auf Nahrungsergänzungsmittel schaffen. Unser Ziel ist es, unsere moderne und innovative liposomale Technologie für jeden zugänglich zu machen.

Um unserem Ziel näher zu kommen, sind wir auf der Suche nach einer/einem:

People and Culture Administrator (w/m/d)

in Teilzeit, 30 Stunden

Aufgaben:

  • Bearbeiten aller operativen HR-Prozesse - vom Recruitment, Onboarding über die Personalbetreuung bis hin zum Exitmanagement

  • Erstellung von Arbeitsverträgen , Bescheinigungen und Arbeitszeugnissen, etc.

  • selbstständige Verwaltung der betrieblichen Altersvorsorge Inhouse

  • Unterstützung in der vorbereitenden Lohnbuchhaltung

  • Kommunikation mit dem Steuerbüro und relevanten behördlichen Einrichtungen

  • Übernahme von spannenden HR-Projekten (in Teamarbeit oder Eigenregie)

  • Schnittstelle zwischen der Führungsebene und unseren Mitarbeitenden

Erforderliche Qualifikationen:

  • mindestens 2-3 Jahre Berufserfahrungen in der Personalsachbearbeitung in Deutschland

  • Grundkenntnisse im Arbeitsrecht und lohnsteuerrechtlichen Themen

  • sehr gute Deutsch- und gute Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift

  • eigenständige, strukturierte und verbindliche Arbeitsweise

  • hohes Engagement und Teamfähigkeit

Gegenseitiger Respekt, Verlässlichkeit und Eigeninitiative sind für uns selbstverständlich.

Warum PlantaCorp:

Wir bieten Dir eine herausfordernde Tätigkeit in einem abwechslungsreichen Umfeld und Dich erwarten eine Open Door Policy sowie flache Hierarchien. In unserem sehr innovativen und dynamischen Unternehmen, welches stark heranwächst, hast Du die Möglichkeit, deine eigenen Projekte umzusetzen und Dich so persönlich weiterzuentwickeln. Mit dem entsprechenden Engagement und einem ausgeprägten Gespür für Qualität hat jeder die Chance auf mehr Verantwortung.

Das bietet dir PlantaCorp:

  • ein internationales und dynamisches Team

  • wöchentlich frisches Obst

  • täglich Kaffee, Tee sowie Milch und Hafermilch

  • zwei kostenlose Nahrungsergänzungsmittel deiner Wahl pro Monat sowie Mitarbeiter-Rabatt auf alle Produkte

  • eine gute Anbindung an den öffentlichen Nahverkehr

  • eine Bezuschussung zu deinem Deutschlandticket

  • kostenfreie Parkplätze direkt vor Ort (nach Verfügbarkeit)

  • wöchentlich Yoga vor Ort

Neugierig?

Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung inkl. Anschreiben, Lebenslauf, Unterlagen zu deinem höchsten Schulabschluss sowie aller vorhandener Arbeitszeugnisse.

title: People Operations & Payroll (Working Student)
descriptionHtml:
People Operations & Payroll (Working Student)

About the team

At SumUp, our People Operations & Payroll team is the engine behind a smooth and reliable employee experience. We manage the full employee lifecycle — from onboarding and contract changes through to offboarding — while supporting accurate and timely payroll across Southern Europe.

In France, recurring operational work is growing across employee lifecycle administration, field sales hiring and payroll coordination. You'll join a hands-on, detail-driven team where operational excellence and employee care go hand in hand.

The role

This is a Working Student position supporting the People Operations & Payroll team in France. You'll take ownership of recurring administrative and payroll support tasks, help keep our data accurate and up to date, and make sure employees and managers get timely, clear support.

This is a great entry point into HR and payroll operations for someone who is organised, reliable, and eager to build real expertise in a fast-moving environment.

What you'll do

Payroll support

  • Help to collect, and organise payroll input data ahead of monthly deadlines
  • Support follow-up with external payroll and benefits providers where relevant
  • Help maintain accurate payroll records and flag missing information or discrepancies

HR administration & employee lifecycle

  • Prepare, update, and archive employment contracts and employee documentation
  • Support onboarding, contract changes, and offboarding processes — ensuring data accuracy and completeness at every step
  • Assist with benefits administration where needed

Employee support & ticket handling

  • Respond to routine employee and manager queries via internal systems and email with clarity and care
  • Manage open tickets and follow up, escalating more complex cases when needed

Data management & process improvement

  • Maintain and update employee data in HR systems and Excel / Google Sheets trackers
  • Perform regular data checks and keep Notion pages and internal documentation up to date
  • Identify repetitive steps, data-quality issues, or bottlenecks in recurring workflows
  • Suggest small process improvements that make day-to-day operations more efficient

What we're looking for

  • Currently studying or recently graduated in HR, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field
  • Fluent in French and English — clear written and verbal communication is essential
  • Strong attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy, especially with sensitive employee and payroll data
  • Basic Excel / Google Sheets skills and confidence working with structured data
  • Organised and reliable — able to manage recurring tasks and meet regular deadlines
  • Comfortable handling confidential information with discretion and good judgement
  • Quick to learn new tools and systems — we work across multiple HR platforms
  • Team player with a hands-on, service-oriented attitude

Nice to have

  • Previous experience or studies in HR, payroll administration, or people operations
  • Interest in payroll processes, HR systems, or process improvement
  • Familiarity with AI tools such as ChatGPT

Why SumUp?

🌎 Work with a truly global, multicultural team from our Barcelona office.

🌈 Be part of a workplace that values diversity and inclusion, where every perspective is respected.

❤️ Access our Employee Assistance Programme for mental health guidance and support when you need it.

Job Application Tip

We recognise that candidates feel they need to meet 100% of the job criteria in order to apply for a job. Please note that this is only a guide. If you don't tick every box, it's ok too because it means you have room to learn and develop your career at SumUp.

title: Personal Assistant
descriptionHtml:
Personal Assistant to the CEO & COO (Up to £55,000 + early stage equity)

Location: London (3 days per week in London office)

About GetGround

GetGround is the UK’s all-in-one property investment platform, helping investors find, finance and structure their UK property investments, all in one place. We’re a fast-growing fintech with a global investor base and a network of partners across lending, mortgage broking, tax, accounting and property management. We’re a team with big ambitions, and we’re looking for someone exceptional to help our CEO & COO make the most of every day.

This role supports both GetGround and the CEO’s wider diary including some family office duties. You’ll be a trusted presence, so discretion and judgement are central to the role.

The role

This is a high-impact, high-trust position at the centre of GetGround. You’ll be the CEO’s right hand, keeping their time, priorities and communications running smoothly so they can focus on leading the company. You’ll work closely with the leadership team as well as a broad range of stakeholders internally and externally. This is much more than diary management: you’ll be a trusted partner, a problem-solver and a gatekeeper.

What you’ll do

  • Manage the CEO’s diary across GetGround and family office commitments, anticipating clashes and protecting time for what matters most

  • Arrange domestic and international travel, including itineraries, bookings and logistics

  • Take minutes and track actions, following up with owners to make sure things get done (where needed)

  • Act as the first point of contact on diary issues for investors, partners, lenders and other senior external contacts

  • Support the administration of family office matters, including coordinating travel/accommodation/miscellaneous items

  • Coordinate leadership team meetings, offsites and company events

  • Handle expenses, invoices and ad hoc projects

  • Manage confidential, personal and commercially sensitive information with complete discretion

About you

Essential

  • Proven experience as a PA, EA or similar at senior or executive level

  • Outstanding organisation and an instinct for prioritising competing demands

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with the polish to represent the CEO externally

  • Absolute discretion and sound judgement with confidential and personal information

  • Proactive and resourceful: you spot problems before they land and solve them quietly

  • Comfortable moving between business and personal or family matters with equal professionalism

  • Confident with Google Workspace and quick to pick up new tools

Desirable

  • Experience in a fast-growing fintech, proptech or financial services business

  • Familiarity with a regulated environment (some GetGround services are FCA-regulated)

  • Experience supporting board or investor relations

  • Comfort with project coordination and basic reporting

What we are building: The first end-to-end real estate investment offering - making the dream of owning real estate more accessible to everyone globally.

Diversity & inclusion at GetGround: We encourage applications from all sections of society and we believe in the criticality of an inclusive culture. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity or any other basis as protected by law.

  • 42% of our employees identify as female or non-specified, 58% as male

  • 22 nationalities represented across offices in 5 countries

  • Our work on Design Accessibility

  • Inclusion is at the heart of our culture - we celebrate and reflect on key D&I and cultural events such as: Black History Month, International Women's Day and Pride

Du bringst bereits erste Erfahrungen im Bereich Performance Marketing mit? Du verfügst über eine analytische Denkweise, bist aber trotzdem kreativ? Dann bist du die perfekte Ergänzung für unser Team!

  • Du steuerst Budgets und Pacing und behältst die Ziel-KPIs deiner Projekte im Blick.

  • Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit unserem Design-Team die Creative Strategy, schreibst Briefings und Ad Copies und bewertest die Performance einzelner Assets.

  • Du stellst sauberes Tracking sicher (Meta Pixel & Conversions API, GA4, Google Tag Manager, Merchant Center) in Abstimmung mit unserem Development-Team.

  • Du analysierst Daten aus verschiedenen Quellen, erstellst monatliche Reports und leitest daraus konkrete Next Steps ab.

  • Du bist direkte:r AnsprechpartnerIn unserer Partnerunternehmen, präsentierst Ergebnisse und übernimmst Verantwortung für deine Accounts.

  • Du beobachtest Wettbewerb, Plattform-Updates und neue Ad-Formate und bringst sie proaktiv ins Team.

Qualifikation

  • Du hast erste Erfahrung mit Paid Social und SEA, Schwerpunkt Meta Ads und Google Ads.

  • Du hast erste Erfahrung mit Shopify, WordPress, Google Analytics 4 und dem Google Tag Manager.

  • Du verstehst E-Commerce-KPIs wie ROAS, CAC, Conversion Rate, AOV und Customer Lifetime Value.

  • Du arbeitest sicher mit Google Sheets bzw. Excel; Erfahrung mit Looker Studio oder Reporting-Tools ist ein Plus.

  • Dein analytisches Gespür lässt dich die richtigen Maßnahmen für deine KundInnen ableiten.

  • Du hast ein Gefühl dafür, was ein gutes Creative ausmacht, und denkst in Hooks, Formaten und Zielgruppen.

  • Du nutzt AI-Tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini etc.) regelmäßig und hast Lust, Workflows damit smarter zu machen.

  • Du arbeitest strukturiert, eigenverantwortlich und mit Hands-on-Mentalität.

Benefits

  • Modernes Office mit Dachterrasse im Herzen Frankfurts

  • Zuschuss für eine Fitnessstudio-Mitgliedschaft

  • Snacks und Getränke aufs Haus

  • Attraktive Rabatte bei unseren Partner-Brands

  • Fortbildungsmöglichkeiten nach deinen Wünschen

title: Platform Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Why Faculty?


We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here.

We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.

Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.

AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

 

About the team

 

Bringing medicine to patients is complex, expensive and high-risk. Faculty’s Life Science’s team is concentrated on building AI solutions which optimise the research and commercialisation of life-changing therapies.

We partner with major pharma firms, academic research centres and MedTech start-ups to design and deliver solutions which address critical healthcare challenges, and help to democratise health for all.

  

About the role

 

We're looking for a Platform Engineer to build the backbone of applied artificial intelligence for our customers. You will design, build, and deploy robust, secure, and scalable cloud infrastructure that powers cutting-edge data and machine learning workflows. Working in a cross-functional team, you'll solve complex challenges and empower our data scientists and ML engineers to deploy their work effectively, shaping the future of AI solutions.

  

What you'll be doing:

 

  • Building robust, secure, and scalable cloud infrastructure for AI and ML workflows.

  • Partnering with technical and non-technical stakeholders, from initial idea generation through to implementation and shipping.

  • Enabling Machine Learning Engineers and Data Scientists by contributing to internal best practices, standards, and reusable code repos.

  • Proactively identifying and recommending new ways customers can leverage cloud infrastructure to solve their key challenges.

  • Creating and maintaining reusable, company-wide libraries and infrastructure-as-code.

  • Researching and integrating the best open-source technologies to enhance Faculty's infrastructure capabilities.

 

Who we're looking for:

 

  • You are pragmatic and outcome-focused, balancing the big picture with the details to execute complex projects in the real world.

  • You think scientifically, always testing assumptions, seeking evidence, and looking for opportunities to improve how things are done.

  • You have a drive to learn, constantly exploring new technologies and novel applications for existing tools.

  • You possess deep experience with both Azure and AWS as well as Infrastructure as Code, especially Terraform.

  • You are experienced in building and deploying containerized solutions using Docker and Kubernetes, supported by strong CI/CD and GitOps practices.

  • You possess proficient knowledge of Networking and Cloud Security

  • You excel at working directly with clients and stakeholders, confidently handling requirements gathering, technical planning, and scoping.

 

The Interview Process

 

  1. Talent Team Screen (30 minutes)

  2. Pair Programming Interview (90 minutes)

  3. System Design Interview (90 minutes)

  4. Commercial Interview (60 minutes)

 

Our Recruitment Ethos

We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.

If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours.

A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI.

title: Post-doctorant·e en Théorie de l’information quantique des systèmes bosoniques - CDD 24 mois
descriptionHtml:
Présentation de Télécom SudParis :

Télécom SudParis est une grande école publique d'ingénieurs reconnue au meilleur niveau des sciences et technologies du numérique. La qualité de ses formations est basée sur l’excellence scientifique de son corps professoral et une pédagogie mettant l’accent sur les projets d’équipes, l’innovation de rupture et l’entreprenariat. Télécom SudParis compte 1 000 étudiantes et étudiants dont 700 élèves ingénieurs et environ de 150 doctorantes et doctorants. Télécom SudParis fait partie de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, premier groupe d’école d’ingénieurs en France, et partage son campus avec Institut Mines-Télécom Business School. Télécom SudParis est co- fondatrice de l'Institut Polytechnique de Paris (IP Paris), Institut de Sciences et Technologies à vocation mondiale avec l’École polytechnique, l’ENSTA Paris, l’ENSAE Paris, l'ENPC et Télécom Paris. Vidéo présentation de Télécom SudParis

À propos de l'Institut Mines-Télécom :

L'Institut Mines-Télécom (IMT) est un établissement public dédié à l'enseignement supérieur et la recherche pour l'innovation dans les domaines de l'ingénierie et du numérique. À l’écoute permanente du monde économique, l'IMT conjugue une forte légitimité académique et scientifique, une proximité avec les entreprises et un positionnement unique sur les transformations majeures au XXIe siècle : numériques, énergétiques, industrielles et éducatives siècle. Ses activités se déploient au sein des grandes écoles Mines et Télécom sous tutelle du ministre en charge de l’Industrie et des communications électroniques, de deux filiales et de partenaires associés ou sous convention. L'IMT est membre fondateur de l’Alliance Industrie du Futur. Il est doublement labellisé Carnot pour la qualité de sa recherche partenariale. Vidéo de présentation de l'Institut Mines-Télécom

Missions

  1. Assurer des missions de recherche en théorie de l’information quantique, avec un accent particulier sur les systèmes quantiques bosoniques

  2. Assurer des missions d’encadrement et de tutorat des étudiants

  3. Contribuer à la notoriété de Télécom SudParis, de l’Institut Mines-Télécom et de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris

Activités

  1. Assurer des activités de recherche en théorie de l’information quantique

  • Étudier les propriétés mathématiques et informationnelles des états et canaux quantiques bosoniques, en mettant particulièrement l’accent sur les systèmes non gaussiens.

  • Étudier et chercher à démontrer des inégalités entropiques quantiques intervenant en théorie de l’information quantique bosonique, notamment des inégalités liées à l’action des diviseurs de faisceau et d’autres transformations bosoniques physiquement pertinentes.

  • Développer de nouveaux outils mathématiques pour l’analyse des états et canaux bosoniques non gaussiens, en s’appuyant notamment sur des méthodes issues de la théorie de l’information quantique, de l’analyse matricielle et des opérateurs, de la théorie de la majorisation et de domaines connexes.

  • Appliquer ces résultats à la caractérisation de la transmission de l’information à travers les canaux quantiques bosoniques, en particulier à l’établissement de formules de capacité ainsi que de bornes supérieures ou inférieures sur les capacités de communication.

  • Explorer les liens entre les méthodes développées et d’autres problématiques de la théorie de l’information quantique et de la physique mathématique.

  • Contribuer à la réalisation des objectifs scientifiques et des livrables du projet de recherche.

  • Présenter et discuter les résultats de recherche au sein de l’équipe ainsi qu’avec des collaborateurs extérieurs.

  • Préparer des publications scientifiques présentant les résultats des travaux de recherche.

2. Assurer des activités d’enseignement, d’encadrement et de tutorat

  • Assurer des séances de travaux dirigés dans le cadre d’un cours de théorie de l’information quantique.

  • Préparer et mettre à jour des feuilles d’exercices, des corrigés et d’autres supports pédagogiques pour ce cours.

  • Encadrer des projets étudiants et, le cas échéant, des stages de recherche.

  • Contribuer à l’accompagnement scientifique de doctorants et d’autres jeunes chercheurs travaillant sur des thématiques connexes.

3. Contribuer à la notoriété de Télécom SudParis, de l’Institut Mines-Télécom et de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris

  • Publier les résultats des travaux de recherche dans des revues internationales à comité de lecture et dans des actes de conférences.

  • Présenter les résultats de recherche lors de conférences internationales, d’ateliers, de séminaires et de rencontres scientifiques.

  • Participer à des collaborations scientifiques avec des institutions académiques et des centres de recherche en France et à l’étranger.

  • Contribuer à l’animation scientifique et à la visibilité du département et de l’établissement.

4. Activités diverses

  • Participer aux activités scientifiques et académiques du département et de l’établissement.

  • Participer aux séminaires de recherche, aux réunions de projet et aux autres activités scientifiques collectives.

  • Rendre compte de l’avancement et des résultats des activités de recherche dont il ou elle a la charge.


Formation

  • Doctorat en physique, mathématiques, informatique, ingénierie, ou dans un domaine connexe pertinent pour la théorie de l’information quantique

  • Expérience de recherche en théorie de l’information quantique, physique mathématique, théorie de la communication quantique, optique quantique théorique, ou dans un domaine étroitement lié

  • Expérience des approches analytiques et mathématiques appliquées à des problèmes de théorie de l’information quantique.

Compétences, connaissances et expériences indispensables

  • Maîtrise de l’anglais écrit et oral.

title: Post-doctorante ou Post-doctorant en transmission et détection sur fibres à cœurs creux - CDD de 18 mois
descriptionHtml:
Qui sommes-nous ?

Télécom Paris, école de l’IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) et membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris, est une grande école du top 6 des écoles d’ingénieurs généralistes françaises.

La Raison d’Être de Télécom Paris est de former, imaginer et entreprendre pour concevoir des modèles, des technologies et des solutions numériques au service d’une société et d’une économie respectueuses de l’humain et de son environnement.

Nous recherchons une Post-doctorante ou un Post-doctorant en transmission et détection sur fibres à cœurs creux pour rejoindre le département COMELEC à Télécom Paris.

Les fibres à cristaux photoniques à cœur creux (Hollow-Core Photonic Crystal Fibers, HCPCF) ont récemment franchi une étape technologique majeure, avec des pertes de propagation pouvant atteindre 0.1 dB/km à 1550 nm, comparables, voire inférieures, à celles des fibres télécoms standards [1–2]. La lumière se propageant principalement dans l’air, les HCPCF présentent une latence réduite de 30 à 40 %, une dispersion ultra-faible et des non-linéarités optiques négligeables. Ces propriétés uniques en font des technologies particulièrement prometteuses pour les systèmes de télécommunications de nouvelle génération, la distribution quantique de clés (Quantum Key Distribution, QKD) sur longue distance et les applications de détection distribuée.

Le projet proposé vise à développer et démontrer la prochaine génération de fibres à cristaux photoniques à cœur creux (HCPCF) pour la transmission de données à haut débit et les applications de détection. La propagation de la lumière dans l’air plutôt que dans le verre permet aux HCPCF d’offrir une latence réduite et des non-linéarités optiques négligeables par rapport aux fibres de silice, répondant ainsi à certains des enjeux majeurs des futurs centres de données et réseaux optiques. Notre ambition est de démontrer une transmission à 400 Gbit/s sur quelques kilomètres à travers des échantillons de fibres issus de nouvelles architectures, et d’étudier le potentiel de ces HCPCF pour des applications de détection. La réalisation de ces objectifs nécessite de répondre à des spécifications exigeantes en matière de guidage monomode, de contrôle de la polarisation, ainsi que de faibles pertes par courbure et par couplage.

Deux équipes complémentaires assureront conjointement l'encadrement de ces travaux : le GPPMM, reconnu internationalement pour ses activités de conception et de fabrication de HCPCF [3–5], et le GTO, leader dans la démonstration de systèmes de communication optique et de détection à haut débit [6–8]. Un processus itératif entre la fabrication des fibres et leur caractérisation au niveau système permettra de s'assurer que leurs propriétés répondent aux exigences opérationnelles en matière de transmission et de détection. Sur le plan méthodologique, le projet combinera modélisation numérique, caractérisation et validation expérimentale dans la bande C. Les méthodes de modélisation et de traitement du signal développées au GTO pour le suivi de la polarisation contribueront à évaluer et à optimiser les performances de transmission des HCPCF conçues et caractérisées au GPPMM.

À propos du projet PLEIADES

Le projet PLEIADES s'inscrit dans le cadre du programme PEPR « Réseaux du futur », financé par l'ANR, et réunit un consortium de 14 partenaires. L'un des axes de travail porte sur les fibres à cœur creux de nouvelle génération et rassemble plusieurs laboratoires académiques, notamment LTCI, XLIM et PHLAM.

Vos principales missions seront de :

  • Assurer des missions de recherche dans le domaine de la photonique

  • Assurer des missions d’encadrement et de tutorat

  • Participer à la notoriété de l’Ecole, de l’Institut Mines-Télécom et de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris


Vous êtes titulaire d’un doctorat ou équivalent en génie électrique, communications, photonique, traitement du signal ou dans un domaine connexe. Vous disposez de solides connaissances en systèmes et réseaux de transmission optique ainsi qu’en traitement numérique du signal (DSP) appliqué aux systèmes de communication ou aux capteurs à fibre optique. La maîtrise de MATLAB et/ou Python pour le développement d’algorithmes DSP sera appréciée. Vous manifestez un intérêt marqué pour la recherche appliquée et êtes à l’aise dans un environnement multiculturel, notamment pour encadrer des stagiaires et/ou des étudiants. Une bonne maîtrise de l’anglais est indispensable. Vous disposez également de bonnes qualités relationnelles et pédagogiques, d’un bon esprit d’équipe et d’une capacité à synthétiser et à communiquer des informations complexes.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Vous travaillerez dans un environnement en plein développement, agréable, verdoyant et accessible (notamment pour les personnes en situation de handicap) à seulement 20 km de Paris (RER B et C, proximité des grands axes routiers).

Vous bénéficierez de :

  • 49 jours de congés annuels (CA + RTT)

  • flexibilité des horaires de travail (en fonction de l'activité du service)

  • télétravail 1 à 3 jours/semaine possible

  • Remboursement abonnement transports en commun à 75%

  • Proximité de nombreuses infrastructures sportives, conciergerie, parking souterrain, restauration interne...

  • A savoir : nos cotisations sociales sont moins élevées que dans le secteur privé

Type d'emploi : CDD de 18 mois

Nos recrutements sont fondés sur les compétences, sans distinction d’origine, d’âge, d'identité de genre et d’orientation sexuel et tous nos postes sont ouverts aux personnes en situation de handicap.

title: Principal Engineer - Identity & Privacy
descriptionHtml:
About Skyscanner

Everyone loves travelling, but planning is not without its challenges ✈️. That's why we've spent 20 years building tools that turn travel-planning chaos into a breeze. Today, around 160 million travellers count on us every month to skip the whole “47 browser tabs open” phase and find flights, cars, and hotels quickly and easily 💻.

Joining Skyscanner means becoming part of a global brand that's striving to become the planet's go-to travel hack accessible for all 🌍.

Our vision? To be the world's number one travel ally. (Ambitious? 💪Yes, but, hey, that's what got us here).

Now, we’re on the lookout for a Principal Engineer - Identity & Privacy to help us bring that vision to even more travellers.

About the role
(Hybrid)

As our Principal Engineer for Identity & Privacy, you’ll shape the technical foundations that help us earn traveller trust while safely unlocking the data and AI capabilities behind brilliant product, personalisation, experimentation and advertising experiences.

This is a senior technical leadership role with impact right across Skyscanner. You’ll own the technical strategy and set standards for identity, consent and privacy engineering across our traveller-facing products, data platforms and operational systems — spanning web, app, backend, experimentation, analytics, advertising and machine learning.

What you’ll be doing

  • Setting our technical strategy: You’ll define and communicate the long-term vision and roadmap for identity, consent and privacy engineering, aligning it with our product strategy, traveller trust goals and data and AI ambitions.

  • Shaping identity at scale: You’ll lead our technical approach to purpose-scoped identifiers and consent-aware data processing across sessions, tracking, advertising, accounts, consent and derived identifiers.

  • Connecting the dots end-to-end: You’ll establish how identity and consent state flows from web and app surfaces through backend services, event streams and data pipelines to downstream consumers — making a complicated ecosystem feel a lot less complicated.

  • Turning privacy into engineering practice: You’ll translate privacy principles and legal guidance into reusable engineering patterns, platform controls, decision frameworks and measurable standards, including clear expectations around retention, deletion, masking, access control and auditability.

  • Leading across Skyscanner: You’ll partner with Engineering, Product, Legal, Privacy, Security, Data Governance, Data Science, Marketing, Ads and Analytics to navigate trade-offs, create clarity and turn ambiguous problems into decisions teams can deliver against.

  • Getting hands-on with the big stuff: You’ll provide technical leadership for large-scale initiatives spanning consent platform capabilities, privacy-safe experimentation, data retention and deletion, and traveller-trust features, while guiding teams towards simple, scalable, reliable and cost-effective solutions.

  • Raising the engineering bar: You’ll use observability, engineering health and incident learnings to improve how we operate, while coaching and mentoring engineers and championing high standards, constructive challenge and inclusive collaboration across our Engineering community.

About you

  • Privacy-engineering experienced: You’ve translated privacy and data-protection requirements — including GDPR, PECR, CCPA/CPRA or equivalent global frameworks — into practical engineering decisions, working effectively with Legal, Privacy, Security and Data Governance partners.

  • Built for scale: You’ve designed, built and operated large-scale distributed systems across identity, data platforms or adjacent areas such as consent, authentication, advertising technology or customer data infrastructure.

  • An influential technical leader: You’ve led significant technical change across multiple teams without direct line authority, creating clarity, alignment and momentum when ownership is distributed.

  • Strong in technical judgement: You’re comfortable making decisions where product value, traveller trust, privacy requirements, operational reliability and cost are all competing for a seat at the table.

  • End-to-end minded: You can reason confidently across client surfaces, backend services, event streams, data products, ML features, analytics, partner exports and operational tooling — and understand how a decision in one part of the system can ripple through the rest.

  • Practical about standards: You know how to turn policy into technical controls and measurable quality standards that teams can consistently use in real systems, rather than another document destined for a forgotten browser tab.

  • Clear, collaborative and credible: You can create shared engineering practices, write clear technical strategy and work effectively with senior stakeholders across Engineering, Product, Legal, Security and Data Governance. Familiarity with privacy and consent technologies, experimentation, personalisation, advertising measurement, Databricks, OpenTelemetry or SQL is valuable but not essential — as is practical experience using AI tools to make engineering work smarter.

What it's like here

We are the real deal - no corporate gloss, no empty promises. Just a team of genuinely curious, caring humans ❤️, building things that help travellers explore the world a little easier 🧭.

Skyscanner is made up of brilliant humans from every corner of the world. We believe travel makes the world better - and that the same is true of our diverse teams. title: Principal Machine Learning Scientist, Recommender Systems
descriptionHtml:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~160 people, around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

Every courier who works with Relay chooses their day. A day is a set of routes that have to fit together, and every courier's ideal day competes with everyone else's. Work is finite and every route still has to be covered, so matching thousands of couriers to the work they want is a recommendation problem with few precedents.

Science at Relay is the brain of the operation: machine learning, operational research, recommender systems, causal inference, location intelligence and experimentation, working together to decide how every parcel gets delivered. There's no existing recommender to iterate on. You'll build it.

Recommender Systems Highlights

  • Combinatorial, constrained and competitive: every recommendation has to be feasible for the whole network, not just right for one courier.

  • Your models power large-scale optimisation that balances thousands of couriers' preferences against the constraints of a physical network.

  • Price is part of the recommendation, so economics, personalisation and optimisation have to work as one.

  • Our apps collect millions of data points every day.

The Opportunity

As a Principal Machine Learning Scientist at Relay, you'll:

  • Set the standard for recommender systems at Relay.

  • Lead the evolution of Relay's recommender from research to production.

  • Design and build the recommender systems that power Relay's key decisions.

  • Partner with Operational Research to unite recommender models and optimisation.

  • Contribute to Relay's research culture, and develop our voice in the tech community.

We're looking for candidates who…

  • Have built recommender systems at scale, owned them in production, and led their direction.

  • Bring deep expertise in recommender systems, reinforcement learning and LLMs, whether from a PhD, publications, or years at the frontier in industry.

  • Think in experiments, and let evidence guide decisions.

  • Are energised by open-ended problems, and know how to make them tractable.

  • Collaborate generously, and explain complex ideas simply.

Don't tick every box? If this problem excites you, we'd still love to hear from you.

Who Thrives at Relay?

  • Aim with Precision: You define problems clearly and measure your impact meticulously.

  • Play to Win: You chase bold bets, tackle the hard stuff, and view constraints as fuel, not friction.

  • 1% Better Every Day: You believe that small, consistent improvements lead to exponential growth. You move quickly, deliver results, and learn from every experience.

  • All In, All the Time: You show up and step up. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts.

  • People-Powered Greatness: You invest in your teammates. You give and receive feedback with care and candour. You build trust through high standards and shared success.

  • Grow the Whole Pie: You seek out win-win solutions for merchants, couriers, and our customers, because when they thrive, so do we.

    If these resonate, and you combine strong technical fundamentals with entrepreneurial drive, let’s connect.

Relay is an equal-opportunity employer committed to diversity, inclusion, and fostering a workplace where everyone thrives.

title: Principal Radio Frequency Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Metrea delivers effects-as-a-service to national security partners across five domains and more than a dozen mission areas. These include airborne ISR, electronic warfare, secure communications, aerial refueling, special air missions, aerial firefighting, and advanced simulation. We own the whole stack: designing, building, and operating turnkey capabilities that give our partners decisive, asymmetric advantage against rapidly evolving threats.

Our operating model is built around three interlocking pillars. The Support Groups provide a global shared-service – spanning people, finance, platform, operations, legal, and engagement. This frees up our Core Groups, who develop and own mission capabilities end-to-end, to focus entirely on delivery. The Market Groups apply a regional lens, ensuring that our agile and adaptable capabilities remain aligned to the wicked problems that matter most to our partners across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific.

At the heart of our model is a simple but powerful idea: be a true partner with skin in the game. Our partners need effects, not just equipment. By owning the full stack – from the lab to the field – we are able to drive a continuous cycle of innovation that keeps our partners ahead. It's a fast-moving, intellectually demanding environment where talented people are given real responsibility, work on problems that matter, and contribute to an enterprise that is growing quickly and deliberately.

Headquartered in Washington, DC, with facilities across the United States, the United Kingdom, as well as Continental Europe and Asia-Pacific.

Group Overview

Electromagnetic and Cyber Group (EM&C) is responsible for developing flexible and survivable advanced electronic warfare and secure communications equipment while providing the industry’s leading signals intelligence, electronic warfare, and cyber experts.  Metrea specialises in signal classification, direction finding, advanced geolocation techniques, and waveform development including waveforms for MANET and LPI/LPD applications. Metrea also develops special purpose radios for government customers and licenses DF and geolocation solutions to multiple OEMs.

The Expeditionary Operations Lab, or EXOLAB, focuses on the rapid development, integration, evaluation and delivery of expeditionary capabilities within the Electromagnetic Warfare and Cyber domain. EXOLAB works across research and development, experimentation, prototyping, systems integration, trials and operational delivery. The team addresses complex customer problems by combining existing technologies, emerging capabilities and internally developed solutions into deployable systems. The lab operates across airborne, land, maritime and dismounted environments, with a strong emphasis on practical engineering, rapid learning and delivering systems that are operationally relevant, supportable and resilient. 

Position Summary

We are seeking a Principal RF Engineer to lead and support the research, design, development, integration and delivery of radio-frequency systems for expeditionary Electronic Warfare, signals intelligence, spectrum operations and secure communications capabilities. 

The role will be responsible for the RF engineering aspects of prototype and operational systems, including RF architecture, receiver and transmitter chains, antenna systems, signal distribution, filtering, amplification, frequency conversion, interference management and system performance analysis. 

The Principal RF Engineer will operate as a senior technical authority within a multidisciplinary team comprising electrical, systems, mechanical, software, cyber and operational specialists. The role will support the full engineering lifecycle, from concept development and technology evaluation through detailed design, integration, verification, trials, deployment and through-life support. 

This is a practical, delivery-focused engineering role. The successful candidate will be comfortable moving between theoretical analysis, simulation, laboratory testing, prototype development, platform integration and field trials. 

The role will be based either in Lincoln or London, with a longer-term intent to transition the primary location to London if hired initially in Lincoln. 

What You'll Do

  • Design, develop and integrate RF systems for expeditionary Unmanned Systems control, Electronic Warfare, signals intelligence, spectrum-monitoring and secure communications capabilities
  • Develop RF system architectures covering antennas, receivers, transmitters, amplifiers, filters, frequency conversion, switching and signal distribution
  • Conduct RF performance analysis, including gain, noise figure, sensitivity, dynamic range, linearity, link budgets and interference assessments
  • Support rapid R&D, prototyping and technology evaluation, translating operational requirements into practical and deployable RF solutions
  • Integrate commercial, government and internally developed RF equipment across airborne, vehicle-mounted, maritime, fixed-site and unmanned platforms
  • Plan and conduct RF testing, characterisation, fault diagnosis, verification and corrective engineering activity
  • Ensure RF designs consider electromagnetic compatibility, spectrum management, grounding, bonding, shielding, environmental protection and relevant standards
  • Work closely with electrical, mechanical, software, cyber, systems and operational teammates throughout the engineering lifecycle
  • Support UK and international trials, demonstrations, installations, commissioning and operational deployments
  • Provide RF technical leadership, design assurance and clear engineering recommendations to customers, suppliers and internal stakeholders

What You Bring

  • Degree in RF Engineering, Electronic Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Telecommunications Engineering or a closely related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience
  • Minimum of seven years’ experience in RF systems design, development, integration, testing or delivery
  • Experience working with complex RF systems within defence, aerospace, telecommunications, Electronic Warfare, signals intelligence, secure communications or a related sector
  • Experience with Software Defined Radios, digital RF architectures and the collection or analysis of IQ data
  • Experience designing, integrating or supporting RF systems for unmanned systems, including uncrewed aerial, ground or maritime platforms
  • Strong understanding of RF receiver and transmitter architectures, including amplifiers, filters, mixers, oscillators, switches and frequency-conversion stages 
  • Experience conducting cascade analysis, link-budget calculations and assessments of gain, noise figure, sensitivity, linearity and dynamic range
  • Practical experience with antenna systems, RF distribution, transmission lines, impedance matching, grounding, bonding and shielding
  • Strong RF test, measurement and fault-finding skills using equipment such as spectrum analysers, vector network analysers, signal generators, oscilloscopes and power meters
  • Experience using RF simulation, modelling, schematic-capture or system-analysis tools
  • Ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary teams spanning electrical, mechanical, software, cyber, systems and operational disciplines
  • Ability to produce clear technical documentation, communicate engineering recommendations and travel regularly within the UK and internationally

Additional Eligibility Qualifications

  • Experience designing expeditionary, deployable, ruggedised or rapidly reconfigurable RF capabilities
  • Experience integrating RF systems onto airborne, vehicle-mounted, maritime, fixed-site or dismounted platforms
  • Understanding of antenna selection, placement, radiation patterns, platform effects and co-site interference
  • Experience with wideband receivers, transmit chains, power amplifiers, low-noise amplifiers, filters and RF switching networks
  • Experience conducting electromagnetic compatibility, electromagnetic environmental effects and radio-frequency interference assessments
  • Familiarity with relevant defence, aviation, maritime, spectrum-management or RF engineering standards
  • Experience supporting prototype builds, field trials, exercises, customer demonstrations or operational deployments
  • Knowledge of systems engineering, size, weight, power and cooling analysis, low-volume manufacturing, component obsolescence and through-life support

Benefits

  • Private medical insurance   
  • Subsidised gym membership / plans through Wellhub   
  • Electric car scheme   
  • Cycle to work scheme   
  • Salary sacrifice pension scheme   
  • Free lunch on office days  
  • Enhanced parental leave  
  • 30 days annual PTO plus bank holidays  

Work Authorization / Security Clearance

The successful candidate must have the right to work in the United Kingdom. 

The role will require the individual to hold, or be capable of obtaining and maintaining, an appropriate UK national-security clearance. Certain projects may impose additional nationality or security restrictions. 

AAP/EEO Statement

Metrea Mission Data Limited is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or other characteristics protected by law.  

Position Type and Expected Hours of Work

This is a full-time position with typical working hours of Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. This position is offered on a hybrid working basis with three days per week in the office as standard, based out of London or Lincoln.

Work Environment

The role will involve work across: 

  • Office and engineering-design environments 
  • Laboratories and workshops
  • Customer and supplier facilities
  • Vehicle, aircraft and maritime-platform integration environments
  • Outdoor test, trial and exercise locations
  • Operationally representative and potentially austere environments  

Appropriate training, procedures and personal protective equipment will be provided where required. 

The role is not exclusively desk-based. It may involve: 

  • Standing, walking, bending, kneeling and working in restricted equipment spaces
  • Handling tools, cables, connectors and test equipment
  • Installing or removing electrical and electronic equipment
  • Lifting and carrying equipment within appropriate manual-handling limits
  • Working around vehicles, aircraft, generators and other powered systems
  • Periods of outdoor work in varying environmental conditions

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with additional needs to perform the essential functions.

Travel

15%

Our Firmware

At Metrea, our single core value is Rooted in Humility, and our four cornerstone attributes are Entrepreneurial, Systematic, Discerning, and Over-Deliver. These form what we call our Teammate Firmware. Just like technical firmware connects software and hardware, our Firmware is the constant interface between our mission and our people. It defines how we show up, how we work together, and how we solve complex problems.

Our team Firmware creates a web-like, hyper-collaborative, dynamically hierarchical way of working that helps us adapt quickly, communicate openly, and distribute decision-making to where expertise actually lives. It enables groups to self-organize around hard problems, shift fluidly as priorities evolve, and operate with the trust, curiosity, and discipline required in a complex mission space. This foundation allows us to deliver elegant, effective solutions and uphold our purpose: protecting our precious inheritance.

title: Product Designer, AI-Native Products (Staff-Level / L6)
descriptionHtml:
Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US.

As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations.

Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow.

The role:

We're looking for a Staff (L6) Product Designer to lead design for some of Synthesia's AI-native, agentic Sessions product surfaces.

Sessions are the experiences where employees learn through conversation, companies lrun a survey at scale, and AI becomes a direct participant in how work gets done - not just a tool behind the scenes.

This area is central to redefining what a video platform can be: moving upstream from content creation into workforce development, and making complex AI capabilities feel natural, trustworthy, and effective for everyday users.

You'll operate as a senior IC: setting direction, influencing roadmap decisions, shaping bets with Product and Engineering leaders, and raising the craft bar.

In practice, this role is about solving AI-native design problems, for example:

  • Designing real-time, conversational avatar experiences that feel engaging and natural - not robotic or gimmicky - for employees learning and practising skills at work.

  • Creating interaction patterns for AI-driven workflows that give users the right amount of control, transparency, and trust without overwhelming them with complexity.

  • Improving output quality through better structure, guidance, and feedback loops - helping users understand what the AI is doing, catch issues early, and iterate with confidence.

  • Working at the frontier where AI changes what "interaction" means, and the best patterns are genuinely still being invented.

In this role you will:

  • Own major AI-native bets end-to-end, from problem framing to shipped outcomes and iteration.

  • Set a design vision for our "Sessions" surface, and influence adjacent product areas to stay coherent.

  • Partner closely with Product and Engineering to define what "great" looks like (principles, quality bar, success metrics) and then drive toward it.

  • Prototype and test interaction models quickly - including novel agentic and conversational patterns - and know when high-fidelity matters.

  • Raise the bar on craft: interaction design, UI quality, systems thinking, and consistency across AI-native experiences.

You should apply if you bring:

  • Significant experience designing complex, high-usage product surfaces - ideally including AI-native products, agentic features, conversational interfaces, or products where the system takes meaningful autonomous action.

  • Strong craft in interaction design and visual design, and a track record of shipping work that measurably improves the product experience.

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity: you can turn unclear and fast-moving problem spaces into crisp direction, and you do not wait for perfect clarity.

  • Systems thinking: you understand how AI capabilities, model constraints, and product architecture shape what's actually possible in the UX - not just what looks good on a screen.

  • Excellent communication in design reviews and cross-functional decision-making contexts.

  • Experience designing workflows where trust, transparency, and user control are central - helping users feel confident in AI-driven outputs rather than confused or excluded.

  • A track record of tackling novel problems in maturing product spaces, and shaping the product from early-stage bets through to execution.

  • The ability to leverage feedback from users and customers to ensure the product continues to meet real needs - including enterprise users with high stakes around quality, compliance, and scale.

At Synthesia we expect everyone to:

  • Own it & Go Direct

title: Product Designer
descriptionHtml:
About Aravis

We are building a vertically integrated, AI-native property operations and financial services business serving landlords and tenants. Letly runs rental homes end to end; Aravis is building the accounts, payments and finance around those relationships.

Our ambition is to make managing money and financing a home radically easier and cheaper. We’re a small, AI-native team in London, building for global scale.

 

The role

You’ll own the user experience of Aravis, turning complex financial tasks into clear, usable journeys. Working directly with the founders, product owners and engineers, you’ll take problems from research through to tested, shipped experiences.

We’re looking for exceptional UX judgement: understanding how people navigate, interpret information, make decisions and recover when something goes wrong.

 

What you’ll own

  • Customer understanding: speak to landlords and tenants, observe how they complete tasks and identify where they struggle.

  • Journeys and information architecture: organise the product and design coherent flows across onboarding, accounts, payments, cards and lending.

  • Interaction design: make balances, fees, choices and transaction states understandable. Design for errors, delays and recovery as carefully as successes.

  • Prototyping and validation: explore alternatives, build interactive prototypes and run usability tests. Refine designs through observed behaviour and evidence.

  • Consistent patterns: develop reusable components and interactions that make the product easier to learn and use as it grows.

 

What we’re looking for

  • An outstanding UX portfolio of shipped products, with case studies showing the problem, your decisions, the testing and what improved.

  • Fluency in Figma, interactive prototyping and design systems, with effective use of AI to explore and test ideas.

  • Strong attention to accessibility, product language and visual clarity.

Experience designing financial products or similarly complex customer journeys is useful.

 

How we work

  • Agency: we move fast, own outcomes, and take responsibility for our work end to end.

title: Product Designer
descriptionHtml:
We started building Marshmallow in 2017. Since then, we’ve grown from 3 to 700+ people, gained unicorn status, raised ~£140M over three funding rounds, turned profitable, insured millions of drivers and lent millions in car loans.

But we’re only just getting started. Our goal is to become one of the largest financial services providers in the world. Over the next 10 years we’ll grow exponentially, not only by scaling our existing products, but also by building new ones.

To achieve our goals we need incredibly ambitious, commercially driven people who never settle for ‘good enough’. Marshmallowers are hungry for autonomy and ownership, and would rather improve than coast. Everyone raises standards and has an impact, with a focus on collective success over self-interest.

We’ve created an environment where curious, tenacious people win and grow together. If that sounds motivating, this could be the place for you.

London (hybrid, 3 days in office)

We are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this position.

Marshmallow makes insurance work for everyone, including people the industry has overlooked. Your difference makes the difference, and we design for it.

We’re looking for a Product Designer to join our Telematics team. Telematics is a key part of Marshmallow’s future that sits within Acquisition and how we grow our user base.

In a nutshell, you’ll help more people get onboarded into Marshmallow by reducing friction in our sign up and activation flow. Longer term, you’ll be part of the team that build customer stickiness by working out how to reward and engage customers for being good drivers. You’ll work with a team that will back you up, and you’ll own problems from day one.

What you’ll be doing

  • Starting with the problem. You’ll shape what we’re solving by doing research with customers, spotting patterns, and turning what you hear into clear themes and needs the team can act on.

  • Designing the whole journey. Wireframes, prototypes, flow to polished screens. You’ll be translating complex concepts into clear, benefit-led experiences. You’ll be thinking about the content on the screen and edge cases too. It’s primarily customer facing, web and app but if your work touches our internal tools, you’ll be thinking about that too.

  • Letting data point the way. You’ll use funnel and analytics data to find where customers get stuck and where we could be causing harm. Then you’ll work with your team to fix it.

  • Building with engineers. You’ll work alongside them from the first idea to what’s shipped. Clear specs and smooth handoffs. If a design tweak is quicker to ship yourself, you can raise the PR.

  • Working in a cross-functional team. Product managers, engineers, operations, data and other designers. You’ll continuously challenge and learn from each other.

  • Bringing stakeholders with you. Acquisition gets a lot of attention here. You’ll form your own opinions, explain your thinking, and keep people in the loop. You won’t be doing it alone, and we’ll help you build the skill.

  • Looking after the design system. Contribute to it, keep things consistent with our brand, and flag anything that doesn’t fit so we can sort it.

  • Using AI every day. For research, analysis and production. Try tools, keep what works, and share it with the team.

You should apply if

  • You have a commercial instinct. You have good gut instinct on what makes a product work and a portfolio that backs up what you’ve shipped having good business impact.

  • You have a proactive mind-set. You look to make continuous improvement to the products that you are working on. You find issues and features, write up tickets and ship them when they’re ready.

  • You are actively using AI. You’ve used AI to optimise your workflow and create efficiency gains whether that’s building prototypes, shipping to production, analysing data or conducting research.
